articles.title: Stanley Tucci has seen your 'overtly sexual' comments on Instagram. So have his kids.
articles.summary: Stanley Tucci on "Masterplan," becoming the internet's boyfriend and why his family calls him "Cinderella."
articles.body:
Stanley Tucci cooks. He dresses well. He drinks wine every day and cleans the kitchen so often that his family calls him Cinderella. You can understand why the internet loves him.

But that confidence is something that came with age.

"I feel more comfortable being myself on camera now," Tucci says in Yahoo's latest Off the Cuff . "So if I alter myself as an actor, it's almost strange in a way now. … The tables have sort of turned."

After decades of memorable transformations — from The Devil Wears Prada 's Nigel to The Hunger Games ' Caesar Flickerman — Tucci has found an audience just as happy to watch him be himself. His food and travel shows, now including National Geographic's Tucci in Italy , helped him settle into that role, with viewers pulling up a virtual chair at the table.

But Tucci doesn't need a TV crew to win audiences over. During lockdown in 2020, his wife, literary agent Felicity Blunt, suggested sharing a video of him making a cocktail on Instagram. "And then everything changed," he laughs.

"It's all my wife's doing," he jokes of his internet-boyfriend status. "I guess she's trying to get rid of me."

He remembers laughing with his older children as they read the decidedly explicit comments in response to the post. "It was very funny for an older man," he says. "It was very flattering."

At home, Tucci is dad to five children: three in their 20s, plus Matteo, 11, and Emilia, 8. While the internet has embraced him as a heartthrob, his family sees him as more of a domestic god. The Cinderella nickname comes from his habit of constantly scrubbing.

"If the kitchen isn't clean, I have great difficulty sort of focusing on anything else," he says.

Tucci's growing ease with himself has changed his ambitions. Some opportunities that would have thrilled him in his 30s no longer hold the same appeal.

"I don't need to do them, and I've lost the desire to do them," he says. "I have other desires that take precedence."

Still, he hasn't exhausted the fun of being someone else. In Masterplan , arriving on Prime Video Oct. 16, Tucci plays a master thief who recruits two unsuspecting strangers — who might be his children — to steal the Mona Lisa. Its funny, weird sensibility reminded him of old heist movies.

Below, Tucci talks about the movie lines that still follow him around, raising children with their own talents and why his approach to living well includes daily exercise … but without skipping happy hour.

You have plenty keeping you busy these days. What has to be on the page to make you think, 'This is worth leaving home for' — and what did you find in 'Masterplan'?

I thought it was very funny. It reminded me of heist movies from the 1970s. There was something sort of innocent about it, in a way, with the exception of some language or behavior. But it was funny. It was funny and weird. And I'd never played a character like that before.

Your character in 'Masterplan' has a very particular idea of what it means to be in a family business. Your son has tried acting. Do any of your kids want to follow in your footsteps, and what advice do you find yourself giving them?

My son did some acting when he was younger, but he's a chef now.

Look, if you're good at it, if you have an innate talent and you want to tell stories for the right reasons, good. If you want to be famous, no. I think particularly nowadays, with social media, we confuse fame and talent.

In 'Masterplan,' you're playing someone who makes a living fooling people. In real life, audiences seem drawn to you because you're comfortable being yourself. Has that confidence always come naturally, or is it something you've grown into?

No, I think I've grown into it from doing the television series, going around Italy. I feel more comfortable being myself on camera now. So if I alter myself as an actor, it's almost strange, in a way, now. The tables have sort of turned.

Your Italy series has introduced you to a whole new audience. How rewarding has that been at this point in your career?

Oh, it's great. It's really great. The number of people who watch that show — I feel very fortunate. We have such a great audience.

But I think what I like about it is that you have people of all ages. You have kids, like 10-year-olds, who love the show, all the way up to people who are 100.

You've been making films that a wide range of audiences can enjoy, including families and different generations. How intentional is that at this point in your career?

It's not intentional at all. If it happens, it happens.

From 'The Devil Wears Prada' to 'The Hunger Games' and now 'Masterplan,' you've played characters people really hold on to. Is there a line people quote back to you that you never expected would follow you around for years?

Well, "Gird your loins," certainly. That's probably the most famous.

You've built a career as an actor, director, writer and now someone people travel — and eat — vicariously through. Has your definition of success and ambition changed from what it was in your 30s?

Oh, yeah, very much so. I'm asked to do things now that, in my 30s, I would die to do. And now I don't want to do them because I don't need to do them, and I've lost the desire to do them. I have other desires that take precedence.

Do you remember a tangible time in your career when that shifted? From needing to do something to wanting to do it?

I think it was when I started doing [ Stanley Tucci: Searching for Italy in 2021]. I became more comfortable within myself, about myself. So I didn't feel the need to pretend not to be me anymore.

And audiences clearly enjoy watching you be yourself. You sort of became one of the internet's first boyfriends. Have you heard that title, and what do you think of it?

I have, yeah. It's all my wife's doing! I guess she's trying to get rid of me.

It was weird. I didn't even know how to use my — still barely know how to use — my phone. We made this video during lockdown, and primarily we made it for Curtis Brown, the agency that my wife works for.

She goes, "Well, maybe we should put it out on Instagram." So I said, "Yeah, I'll do it." And then everything changed.

It was very funny. I remember during lockdown sitting around with my older kids and reading out some of the comments. And we laughed so hard because they were all so overtly sexual! It was very funny for an older man. It was very flattering.

The internet sees this suave man who can cook, dress and generally live well. If I were talking to your wife or your kids, what would they say is missing from that picture?

Oh, God, so much. So much. But they call me Cinderella in my house, if I'm there, because I'm constantly cleaning — the kitchen in particular.

I can't help myself. I must clean the kitchen three times a day because I'm always using it, and someone's always in there doing something. And if the kitchen isn't clean, I have great difficulty sort of focusing on anything else.

Now the internet is going to fall in love with you even more. My husband should take notes.

You have Gen Z kids and Gen Alpha kids. What has each generation introduced you to that you wouldn't have discovered on your own?

Well, I think having kids of disparate ages has shown me that children are born who they are. I can't speak to Gen Z and Gen whatever the — I can't remember what's what. But people are born who they are.

And then it's up to you as a parent to encourage them to be happy, healthy and safe, and to always make use of their assets and not be afraid of their faults.

People look to you for advice on healthy living. There are so many supplements, peptides and elaborate morning routines. What does your approach to staying healthy look like?

I exercise every day. I eat well. I don't eat processed foods. I don't eat sugar, only because it doesn't really agree with me. I don't snack a lot. And I have wine every day.

This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

articles.title: Angine de Poitrine is weird. That may be exactly what your brain craves.
articles.summary: Québécois rock duo Angine de Poitrine has gone viral for its bizarre costumes and unconventional music, earning praise from rock legends. A cognitive neurosc...
articles.body:
Meet Khn and Klek de Poitrine, the mysterious Québécois duo behind Angine de Poitrine. Known for their microtonal sound, oversize papier-mache masks and black-and-white polka-dot costumes, the musicians have become an unlikely internet sensation by performing as 333-year-old alien time travelers.

The duo has gone viral over the past year, earning praise from high-profile rock musicians like Dave Grohl and Lars Ulrich , and they even opened for Jack White back in July. Now, they're taking their otherworldly act on a European tour , with sold-out shows drawing fans eager to see the spectacle.

Do they look or sound familiar? You may have encountered them on your social media feed. Perhaps there's a certain je ne sais quoi that makes you want to keep watching them play. You're not alone.

At first glance, Angine de Poitrine looks like a surrealist art project that somehow wandered onto a rock stage. But beneath their avant-garde costumes is a technically ambitious musical act that blends intricate rhythms, looping guitar riffs and unusual pitches into a sound that's as hypnotic as it is hard to categorize.

Who are these mysterious musicians, what exactly are they playing, and why can't people seem to look away? Yahoo explains.

Angine de Poitrine doesn't describe itself as a band, but rather as a "mantra-rock Dada Pythago-Cubist orchestra." The group's name translates from French to "angina pectoris," a medical term for chest pain. Makes sense once you listen to them.

The anonymous musicians behind the rock duo from Saguenay, Quebec, perform under aliases: Khn de Poitrine plays a double-necked guitar and bass, and Klek de Poitrine is on the drums. Onstage, they communicate by forming triangles with their hands, both to each other and the crowd, and by making alien-like grunts and sounds. Their real names have never been publicly confirmed. All we know is that they're not Lady Gaga or Elton John — they're just "two random dudes," as they told the Guardian .

The anonymity started off as something of a joke in 2019. Their main band was booked twice in a week at the same venue in their small hometown, and the musicians didn't think anyone would want to see the same act perform again so soon, they told the Guardian. Lucky for them, the duo had a microtonal side project and just needed a disguise.

Their previous main band made massive papier-mache piñatas for the crowd to destroy in the pit at shows, sparking the idea of creating DIY masks to conceal their identities.

And the polka-dot aesthetic? That came from a spare guitar neck Klek used to build the duo's first microtonal guitar. It was covered in polka dots from the previous owner, and the two ran with the look.

Add comedically long noses into the equation, and the result is a visual identity that's … hard to forget.

But don't let the visual absurdity distract you. Angine de Poitrine's sound is built around microtonal music, which is hardly anything new. The technique uses pitches that fall between the notes of the 12-tone system commonly heard in Western popular music and has a long history in musical traditions across the Middle East and Asia.

They aren't the first Western musicians to experiment with microtones, either. Radiohead, King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, Steve Vai and Jacob Collier are just some other musicians who have done this, too, according to Guitar World .

Khn's custom double-necked guitar and bass divide each octave into 24 notes rather than the usual 12, allowing him to play quarter tones. Because he can't play both instruments simultaneously, he records riffs live into a looper pedal and stacks them in real time, which helps set the rock duo apart.

Playing such a technically demanding instrument with little room for error while wearing an oversize mask adds another challenge, which is why Khn uses visual markers on the frets.

Klek's tight drumming holds everything together, navigating unusual time signatures such as 7/8, 10/4 and 17/4.

The two members of Angine de Poitrine met in their early teens through a mutual friend and were developing their sound years before their breakthrough came online.

Seattle radio station KEXP recorded Angine de Poitrine performing at the Trans Musicales festival in Rennes, France, in December 2025. The station uploaded the session to YouTube in February 2026, and the footage began circulating across social media.

By late March, clips from the performance went viral, accumulating more than 7.5 million views on YouTube and 6 million on Instagram, according to KEXP . At the time of writing this article, the video has amassed 20 million views.

Online, musicians, guitar enthusiasts and music commentators can be seen breaking down the duo's microtonal guitar sound, unusual time signatures and looping techniques.

The duo's appeal has extended beyond social media. Last month, Angine de Poitrine made their U.S. TV debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , performing a new song called "Zugzegk."

The costumes may be what initially stops people mid-scroll, but Robert Zatorre, a professor at McGill University's Montreal Neurological Institute, who specializes in the brain's musical processing, believes the style of music offers a compelling explanation for why viewers keep coming back.

"People tend to like music which is neither too repetitive and predictable and boring, nor music that is too completely chaotic and random," he told Yahoo. "There's sort of a sweet spot between those two streams where there's some structure that you can discern, but there's also some novel theme."

Angine de Poitrine, he said, occupies an interesting position on that spectrum. Its music is complex enough to sound chaotic at first, but repeated musical patterns give listeners something to latch onto.

"It's quite complicated," Zatorre said. "And at first glance, it sounds a bit chaotic. On the other hand, when you actually listen to it carefully, it turns out there are some elements that are repeated frequently, and so that helps."

Why are more people being drawn to them?

In response to the band's performance on Fallon, one commenter wrote, "This music scratches a musical itch in my brain that I didn't even know I had."

There's a scientific explanation for that feeling, according to Zatorre.

"The brain likes to discover novelty," he said. "It likes new things. It likes to be able to learn."

Music we enjoy activates the brain's reward system, he explained, eliciting a pleasurable response. And that might be why the band's music has struck such a chord with listeners.

"In this Ai stuffed internet, I feel like their music is super refreshing. I love the new jam!" one YouTube commenter said.

Zatorre pointed out that the duo's appeal isn't purely musical. Its outlandish costumes and fictional alien personas are also part of the draw. He said the band deliberately challenges the traditional image of a rock star — one who is tough or glamorous. Instead, Klek and Khn's oversize masks and polka dots poke fun at rock-star conventions while their playing style demonstrates technical ability.

"Part of their novelty is that they're shedding the traditional look of rock bands," Zatorre said. "They're very iconoclastic in that sense. They're breaking the tradition, and they're even making fun of tradition."

That contrast may be exactly what makes the duo compelling to many people. The performance looks absurd, but the musicianship is anything but.

One commenter put it simply, "Don't let the costumes fool you. Their skills are off the chart! One of the most exciting things to happen to music in a long time."

articles.title: Lori Loughlin’s Divorce Takes A New Turn As Estranged Husband Requests Spousal Support And Specifies Reason For Their Split
articles.summary: Lori Loughlin’s divorce from fashion designer Mossimo Giannulli has taken another turn after he filed his response to the actress’s […]
articles.body:
Lori Loughlin 's divorce from fashion designer Mossimo Giannulli has taken another turn after he filed his response to the actress's petition to end their nearly 29-year marriage.

The fashion designer, 63, filed his response on Thursday, October 15, confirming that he also wants to dissolve the marriage.

Lori Loughlin, 62, first filed for divorce in September after the couple reportedly separated in August 2025, following years of public scrutiny due to their involvement in the 2019 college admissions scandal.

Mossimo Giannulli Requests Spousal Support Decision

Giannulli filed his divorce response on Thursday, October 15, in Los Angeles Superior Court, formally setting out his position as the couple moves toward ending their marriage.

According to court documents obtained by Star , the 63-year-old fashion designer cited "irreconcilable differences," the same reason given by Loughlin when she filed for divorce in September.

However, his filing included requests concerning financial support that could become important as the proceedings continue.

Giannulli asked the court to "determine whether spousal support shall be payable to either party upon a request of either party." He also requested that the judge decide whether one spouse should contribute toward the other's legal fees.

Giannulli also stated that the extent of Loughlin's separate property, his own assets and debts, and the couple's shared property were not yet known to him. He indicated that he hoped to amend his filing once the relevant information became available.

His response further included an order requiring both parties to disclose financial records covering their income, expenses, separate and shared property, and outstanding debts.

Lori Loughlin Reportedly Wanted Nothing to Do With Her Estranged Husband

The couple's separation was publicly confirmed in October 2025, when a representative for Loughlin said they were living apart but that no legal proceedings were underway at the time.

That same month, a source close to the Full House actress claimed she had reached a breaking point in the relationship.

Lori wanted "nothing to do with" Giannulli, the insider told Page Six , alleging that the designer had used her for years.

The source further claimed Loughlin had hoped he would change after leaving prison but felt his behavior had worsened.

The insider also alleged that discovering messages and emails on Giannulli's phone was the tipping point in their relationship.

Loughlin is reportedly " thrilled" to move forward in her career .

Prenuptial Agreement Could Become Important in Divorce

The couple's financial arrangements could be another significant aspect of the proceedings, particularly because they entered into a prenuptial agreement before marrying.

Loughlin referenced the agreement in her original divorce petition, requesting that their property, assets and debts be divided according to its terms.

According to Page Six , the agreement was signed approximately one month before their November 1997 wedding and amended in August 2015.

Giannulli's latest filing, however, did not specifically mention the prenuptial agreement.

College Admissions Scandal Added Pressure to Their Marriage

Loughlin and Giannulli's separation followed years of intense public scrutiny, including their involvement in the college admissions scandal that emerged in 2019.

Their relationship faced intense public scrutiny in 2019 when they became embroiled in the college admissions scandal, also known as Operation Varsity Blues. The couple admitted to paying $500,000 to help secure their daughters' admission to the University of Southern California through fraudulent athletic recruitment claims.

Both subsequently pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges and served prison sentences in 2020. Loughlin served two months in prison, while Giannulli received a five-month sentence.

The scandal placed considerable pressure on their family and became a defining episode in their public lives.

A source quoted by Star suggested that the fallout contributed to the breakdown of their marriage, claiming Loughlin believed Giannulli had attempted to shift responsibility onto her.

"She tried very hard to make it work after the whole college admissions nightmare, but by all accounts, he tried to push blame onto her," the source revealed. "Apparently, he would tell friends that she was the one pushing for it, which she swears was not the case."

Lori Loughlin Is Reportedly Ready to Move On From The Marriage

As the divorce proceedings continue, a source close to Loughlin has suggested that the actress is eager to bring the marriage to a formal end.

"It's taken longer than she would have liked to get to this point," the source told Star in September. "She is definitely more than ready to tie everything up with Mossimo and be able to cleanly move on with her life."

The source further claimed that Giannulli had been delaying the process because he wanted to reconcile, adding that people close to Loughlin believed she had already moved on emotionally.

The insider also alleged that the way Giannulli behaved after their initial separation affected the actress's willingness to repair the relationship.

"The way he acted after they first split snuffed out any last flicker she had for him," the source added. "She carried herself with respect for their union of all those years, and he did not."

Giannulli has reportedly been spotted with younger stylist Hannah Harrison since the separation, adding to public interest in his personal life.

articles.title: FRRO Mumbai issues show-cause notice to Imran to cancel OCI tag over presence at stir site
articles.summary: FRRO Mumbai issues second notice to US actor Imran Khan, seeking reply on why his OCI status should not be cancelled over protest participation.
articles.body: MUMBAI: After issuing actor Imran Khan a leave India notice on Oct 14, Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), Mumbai, on Saturday sent him a second notice, this time asking him to show-cause why his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status should not be cancelled.Khan, a US national, was granted OCI cardholder status on Dec 15, 2006. To decide if OCI registration should be cancelled, Centre views as relevant the “nature and circumstances” of activities undertaken in India and their implications.The notice cites his presence at the August Kranti Maidan protest in support of CJP’s anti-CEC stir in Delhi. The notice says no police permission was granted for the protest and a case was registered against him and other protesters for unlawful assembly.Also read: 'Made scapegoat, was curious about crowd': What actor Imran Khan's plea saysFRRO has sought his reply in 15 days as the law provides for a hearing before any action is taken to revoke an OCI card under the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955.FRRO acknowledges, though, that the FIR registration and detention by themselves are not conclusive proof of the allegations or an automatic ground for cancellation of his OCI registration, nor does participation, by itself, establish a ground for cancellation.However, FRRO said, the nature, circumstances and implications of acts on the interest of the public, and the OCI’s conduct, are to be examined, where relevant, to see if registration should be cancelled under section 7D of the Citizenship Act.The Citizenship Act Section 7D (e) empowers revocation of OCI in the interests of the sovereignty, integrity of India and security of India, friendly relations with any foreign country, or in the interests of the general public. Centre said it was of the “provisional opinion” that Khan’s registration as an OCI Cardholder may be liable to cancellation under this section, subject to his reply and explanations.FRRO cited an SC ruling to say national security falls under a “broad range of public interests” when legal powers are directed towards the protection of the interests of the state and the public, based always on facts as well.Khan’s advocate Zulfiquar Memon of MZM Legal said, “As his legal representatives, we are currently examining the contents of the new show-cause notice issued to Imran and we look forward to complying and cooperating with the FRRO in terms of replying to the notice. However, we will take this point up before the high court when the matter comes up for hearing so that we get clarity on the status of the earlier issued leave India notice in light of this new show-cause notice issued by the FRRO.”Centre said his participation, detention and related circumstances warrant scrutiny on whether his continued OCI status is consistent with the interests of the general public, and has factored in the distinction between Indians and OCIs and the limited and regulated rights available to OCIs.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Carrot Top Breaks Silence After Suicide Attempt
articles.summary: Carrot Top shared his first public comments since he was hospitalized after a suicide attempt on Sept. 18: "Thank you for being there for me during this time...
articles.body:
Nearly a month after the comedian (real name Scott Thompson ) was hospitalized in Las Vegas following a suicide attempt in Las Vegas, he spoke out for the first time, thanking fans for their support.

"I'm truly overwhelmed by the outpouring of love, support, prayers, and well wishes I've received over the past couple of weeks," Carrot Top shared on Instagram Oct. 17 alongside a photo of him smiling on stage. "Every message, text, and kind thought has meant more to me than you know."

"While I haven't been able to respond to everyone individually, please know that I've felt your love and appreciate each and every one of you from the bottom of my heart," he added. "Thank you for being there for me during this time. It truly means the world to me!"

Additionally, the 61-year-old shared that he'll be returning to the stage on Oct. 19 to perform his nightly comedy special, which he's hosted at the Luxor Hotel and Casino for over 20 years.

Carrot Top was admitted to the hospital on Sept. 18 after a suicide attempt.

In an update shared two days later , his rep said in a statement to TMZ that the Dennis the Menace Strikes Again star was "breathing on his own and continuing to improve, surrounded by his family and those closest to him."

At the time, the rep also added that Carrot Top had been reading the "many messages from fans" while in the hospital, including "stories from people about how his comedy helped them through difficult periods in their own lives."

Along with fans rallying behind him, the Luxor Hotel and Casino publicly expressed its support for the Smiley Face star.

"Scott is a beloved member of the Luxor and MGM Resorts family, and we are relieved to hear that he is recovering," the Luxor Hotel and Casino told KLAS following Carrot Top's hospitalization. "We are thinking of him and wish him strength as he receives the care and support he needs."

On Sept. 26, Carrot Top was released from the hospital , his rep confirmed to NBC News .

Following his much-anticipated return to the stage on Oct. 19, the Chairman of the Board actor has almost daily shows scheduled for the rest of the year, according to the Luxor Hotel and Casino's website .

Although Carrot Top's comedy career has spanned nearly four decades, he's continued to keep a rather low profile outside of his shows.

Still, he's previously shed light on his relationship with honing his craft.

"I think you learn the craft a little bit more, you get a little more confident," Carrot Top explained on the Whiskey Ginger podcast in 2023. "I love writing. I love trying new jokes every night. I'll try five or six things even if they eat s--t, I do them and my crew always knows—they love that part of it."

"I hate when comics just do the same s--t forever don't try to be creative," he added. "Eating it is part of growing as a comic."

For a look back at Carrot Top's comedy career, keep reading…

For the latest breaking news updates, click here to download the E! News App

images.caption: Ethan Miller/Getty Images

Carrot Top was born in Rockledge, Florida, in 1965. But before he got his iconic moniker, he was known as Scott Thomspon . As for the story behind his stage name? "Unfortunately, I had something to do with that," he told Allison Kugel during a 2022 appearance on her Allison Interviews web series. "It's a blessing and a curse. Why I did it? I don't know. I thought the name Scott Thompson was kind of boring. Well, not kind of, it is ." That's why when he decided to pursue a career in comedy in the late 1980s, he wanted a name that would stick.

"Being a stage performer, I always thought I should have something fun," he explained. " Queen Latifah was taken, and so I thought, 'Gosh, I need something better.' I went up to the stage one night and said, 'Bring me up as Carrot Top.' They said, 'Carrot Top? Are you sure?' I said, 'Yes, I'm pretty sure.' And that was it." He added, "I was 'Carrot Top' forever."

Carrot Top had his big break during a 1991 appearance on Comic Strip Live followed by a performance on Star Search , a talent competition show that originally aired from 1983 to 1995 before Netflix rebooted the series in 2026. But his 1992 appearance on Jay Leno 's The Tonight Show marked a turning point in the comedian's career, catapulting him into mainstream stardom. But as the performer climbed the ranks of Hollywood, he learned that with success came public scrutiny.

"If you read what people say about you, it will kill you," he told Esquire in 2015. "Don't do that. But I know some people say I'm hideous, the most disgusting, ugliest guy in the world. And then some people say, 'Oh my God, he's f--king beautiful.'" "I've always been love or hate," he added. "That's fine. Thank God I've had more love than hate."

While the challenges that come with fame may ebb and flow, the entertainer previously shared his determination to stay focused on his craft. "There's a lot of responsibility that goes in with. If you're going to be famous, it's more about the job," he said during a November 2023 appearance on Jason Tartick 's Trading Secrets podcast. "Being famous is silly. But you don't really find out until you probably are. And then you're like, 'This is silly.'
It's also important to have a sense of humor when living in the public eye. As he jokingly added, "And I'm not famous. I'm recognizable in a lineup."

Yes, Carrot Top's unmissable hairdo is in fact natural. After all, he told Bill Maher during a 2023 appearance on the Club Random Podcast that his locks are "all mine." Though he used to rock a fire red curly afro back in the day, he now rocks a "dreaded" look, which he shared was a reflection of his mental health. "It's dreaded because I dread every f--king day of my life being Carrot Top. So, I dread it," he said before adding of his words, "That's actually funny."

As for why he prefers for his locks to grow wild? Well, after Shania Twain asked him why he doesn't put on a hat to cover his hair, he recalled to NPR in 2022 that "I said, No, I like my hair! I don't wanna be stuffed into a hat." "I like being Carrot Top, I don't have a problem with being Carrot Top," he added. "I don't mind being me."

articles.title: Bombom de chocolate com cebola: doce exótico de atrai turistas em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Doce foi criado por engenheira de alimentos em Ituporanga, cidade conhecida como Capital Nacional da Cebola. Unidade custa R$ 4 e desperta curiosidade de moradores e turistas.
articles.summary: O bombom de cebola criado em Ituporanga custa R$ 4 e atrai turistas curiosos com uma receita agridoce que homenageia a Capital Nacional da Cebola.
articles.body:
🍫 Um bombom de chocolate com recheio de cebola é alvo de curiosidade e virou até atração turística em Ituporanga , no Vale do Itajaí, em Santa Catarina .

A iguaria foi criada pela engenheira de alimentos Adriana Corrêa Bittencourt, dona de uma marca de chocolates artesanais no município, conhecido como a Capital Nacional da Cebola.

Ela contou ao g1 que a mistura surgiu para homenagear os colonizadores locais durante o primeiro Festival Gastronômico do município. Três anos depois, segue sendo vendida por R$ 4 a unidade.

“Em um primeiro momento, pensei em desistir diante de algumas caras feias sobre o que poderia dar disso. Mas depois das aulas e direcionamentos do Sebrae, o chef me disse: 'por que não'?. Foi aí que fui para a cozinha testar”, disse.

🧅De acordo com o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), Ituporanga produziu 168 mil toneladas de cebola em uma área de 4,8 mil hectares em 2025, e ficou na segunda posição entre os maiores produtores do país.

Bombom de cebola foi criado por empresária em Ituporanga — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A receita leva cebola roxa caramelizada, processo utilizado para reduzir a acidez do vegetal.

Depois, o ingrediente é misturado a uma ganache de chocolate 40% cacau (cuja receita a empresária mantém em segredo 🤐).

A preparação é finalizada com a trufagem do bombom.

A reação de quem experimenta o doce é uma das partes mais divertidas da experiência, segundo Adriana. Enquanto alguns demonstram receio, outros ficam curiosos para descobrir o sabor da combinação.

Entre os comentários mais inusitados, a empresária já ouviu comparações com hambúrguer e relatos de pessoas que aprovaram o doce, mas disseram que não o comeriam novamente.

Também há quem afirme não gostar da receita. Entre as crianças, algumas chegam a confundir o recheio com manga. O sabor final, no entanto, é agridoce.

"A receita combinou justamente com o chocolate 40%. Ela não combinou com o chocolate ao leite, combinou com uma versão de chocolate meio amargo", conta.

Com o passar dos anos, a curiosidade do público passou a influenciar a criação de novos sabores.

De acordo com Adriana, após três anos do lançamento, os pedidos por experiências diferentes se tornaram mais frequentes, incluindo versões com mais cebola ou com toque picante. Há inclusive turistas que chegam à loja convictos do pedido: bombom de cebola.

De acordo com Adriana, três anos após o lançamento, os pedidos por experiências diferentes se tornaram mais frequentes. Há até turistas que chegam à loja já certos do que querem: experimentar o bombom de cebola que viram nas redes sociais.

Há também turistas que chegam à loja decididos a experimentar o doce que viram nas redes sociais. “Hoje, dentro da loja, a procura às vezes é só pelo bombom. As pessoas entram e falam: ‘Eu vim para comprar o bombom de cebola’. E acabam levando apenas ele”, diz.

articles.title: 'Aquarelas' de Ary Barroso e Tom Jobim colorem com a bossa brasileira o show de Dionne Warwick no Rio de Janeiro  | G1
articles.body:
Dionne Warwick canta músicas como 'Garota de Ipanema', 'Na Baixa do Sapateiro' e 'Aquarela do Brasil' em show na casa Vivo Rio, no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — Foto: Ricardo Nunes / Divulgação Vivo Rio

♬ Poucas cantoras norte-americanas tiveram ou têm um ligação tão forte e permanente com a música brasileira como Dionne Warwick, artista que descortinou todo um universo pop ao gravar, a partir de 1962, uma série de canções da dupla de compositores Burt Bacharach (1928 – 2023) e Hal David (1921 – 2012).

Na década de 1990, precisamente a partir de 1993, Dionne começou a circular por Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e de Salvador (BA), passando temporadas nessas cidades enquanto gravava um álbum com músicas brasileiras, “Aquarela do Brasil”, disco produzido por Téo Lima, batizado com o nome do antológico samba-exaltação de Ary Barroso (1903 – 1964) – gravado por Dionne na versão em inglês escrita por Bob Russell (1914 – 1970) em 1942 e intitulada “Brazil”– e lançado em 1994 com repercussão comercial muito aquém do esperado pela cantora, efeito creditado pela artista ao pouco investimento da gravadora Arista na promoção do álbum.

A intensa relação de Dionne Warwick com a música do Brasil ficou evidenciada mais uma vez no roteiro do show apresentado pela cantora na casa Vivo Rio, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), na noite de ontem, sábado, 17 de outubro.

A apresentação faz parte da perna brasileira da turnê mundial de despedida de Dionne, “Over and out – A farewell tour”, ainda em rotação pelo Brasil e com apresentações agendadas em Porto Alegre (RS) e Curitiba (PR).

A cantora norte-americana Dionne Warwick se despede do palcos do Brasil com o show da “Over and out – A farewell tour” — Foto: Ricardo Nunes / Divulgação Vivo Rio

A dois meses de completar 86 anos, em 12 de dezembro, Dionne Warwick tem usado inteligentemente a voz em tons mais baixos que se ajustam à bossa brasileira.

Na estreia carioca da turnê, a artista recorreu a essa bossa em bloco com músicas do Brasil em versões em inglês. A primeira foi “Garota de Ipanema” – samba apresentado em show pelos compositores Antonio Carlos Jobim (1927 – 1994) e Vinicius de Moraes (1913 – 1980) no mesmo ano de 1962 em que Dionne lançou o primeiro single solo com uma canção de Burt Bacharach e Hal David, “Don't make me over” – na versão em inglês escrita em 1963 por Norman Gimbel (1927 – 2018).

Na sequência, um batuque ancestral introduziu um dos sambas mais famosos de Ary Barroso, “Na Baixa do Sapateiro” (1938), cantado por Dionne em inglês na versão de Ray Gilbert (1912 – 1976) intitulada “Bahia”, em clima de bossa nova, arriscando alguns versos em português como “Meu Senhor do Bonfim / Arranje uma morena igualzinha para mim”.

Em seguida, a cantora reproduziu parte do medley de músicas de Tom Jobim com que abriu o já mencionado álbum “Aquarela do Brasil”. No medley com jeito de pot-pourri, Dionne encadeou trechos de “Quiet nights of quiet stars (Corcovado)” (Antonio Carlos Jobim, 1960, em versão inglês de Gene Lees, 1965), “Wave” (Antonio Carlos Jobim, 1967) e “Waters of march” (Antonio Carlos Jobim, 1972).

Fechando o bloco brasileiro do roteiro do show da “Over and out – A farewell tour”, Dionne Warwick pintou uma “Aquarela do Brasil” de tonalidade quase épica, fazendo gingar com bossa o Brasil do amor dessa grande cantora norte-americana.

A artista encerrou a elegante apresentação reafirmando o amor pelo país e dizendo que o público carioca não iria mais ouvi-la cantar no palco, mas que ainda iria vê-la no shopping center, na praia, enfim, na vida que Dionne Warwick ainda pretende viver no Brasil após sair de cena.

Dionne Warwick inclui medley com músicas de Tom Jobim (1927 – 1994) no roteiro do show da 'Over and out – A farewell tour' — Foto: Ricardo Nunes / Divulgação Vivo Rio

articles.title: ‘This film will be a big hit’: Vijay Deverakonda says his and Rashmika Mandanna starrer ‘Ranabaali’ will be one of the best Telugu films of 2026 despite mixed reviews and a drop in box-office collections

articles.body: Vijay Deverakonda has expressed confidence in his period drama ‘Ranabaali’ despite its mixed response from audiences and critics. The actor believes the Rashmika Mandanna-starrer will be remembered as one of the best Telugu films of 2026, insisting that the project was made to tell an important story rather than simply achieve big box-office numbers. He also praised director Rahul Sankrityan’s storytelling and said the film has several layers for audiences to discover.Vijay Deverakonda says ‘Ranabaali’ will be one of the best Telugu films of 2026Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna’s period drama ‘Ranabaali’ has received a mixed response from audiences and critics. Amid the varied reviews, Vijay has spoken about his expectations from the film, saying he believes it will be remembered as “one of the best Telugu films of 2026”.According to The Indian Express, the actor made the remarks at a press meet on Friday after watching the film the previous night. He said the project holds a special place in his career and could leave a lasting impact on Telugu cinema.“When I watched the film yesterday, I felt that it would be one of the best Telugu films of the year. I had said during the pre-release event that this film would make Telugu cinema proud,” he said.The actor also reflected on how certain films continue to define an artist’s career, even after they have worked on several projects. Referring to ‘Ranabaali’ as his 14th film, he said some performances and stories remain with audiences long after their release.“For all of us, when we look back at our filmographies — this is my 14th film — even after making 25 or 30 films, there will be certain films that people will talk about forever. The impact of those films and the performances in them will remain in people’s hearts,” he added.Vijay Deverakonda says ‘Ranabaali’ was made for a bigger purposeDespite the film’s box-office performance, Vijay maintained that the team had a larger purpose in bringing ‘Ranabaali’ to the screen. According to the actor, the project was not conceived simply to secure a hit or deliver high collections.“And this film, too, will be a big hit. I can see how it is doing, how you are receiving it, how deeply it has impacted you and how passionately you are talking about it. I have been reading your messages and reviews, sharing some of them and enjoying your reactions. You have taken this film forward,” he said.Vijay also praised director Rahul Sankrityan for the way he presented the story and developed its different layers. He said the team considered the subject important enough to tell, regardless of the commercial expectations surrounding the release.“But when we made it, we had something else in mind. We did not make this film merely to deliver a hit or achieve huge box office numbers. Its purpose was much bigger. We felt this was a very important story to tell our people. When you watch the film, you will discover so many layers to its world,” he said.‘Ranabaali’ box office collection: Film sees a drop on day 2According to Sacnilk, ‘Ranabaali’ collected Rs 7.30 crore in India net collections on Saturday, October 17. This represented a 21.1% decline from its reported opening-day collection of Rs 9.25 crore. The film’s worldwide gross collection reportedly reached Rs 26.65 crore after two days in theatres.While the second-day figures indicated a drop in domestic collections, Vijay’s comments suggest that he remains confident about the film’s long-term impact and the story it sets out to tell.‘Ranabaali’ cast and director‘Ranabaali’ stars Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna in the lead roles and is directed by Rahul Sankrityan. articles.title: Kate Cassidy shares emotional tribute to late Liam Payne: 'Until the next life, I’ll see you again one day'

articles.body: Kate Cassidy has shared a tribute to Liam Payne two years after he passed away, looking back on some of her last memories with him. The influencer posted a throwback video of the two of them, with a heartfelt note about cherishing the time you have with the people you love. It showed how much the relationship still means to her, and it got people talking about their memories again.Payne passed away on October 16, 2024, at age 31 after falling from a hotel balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina. On the second anniversary, Cassidy turned to social media to remember their time together, focusing on a playful moment that had since taken on a more emotional significance.Kate Cassidy remembers her final moments with Liam PayneIn a video shared on her official Instagram account on October 16, Cassidy and Payne can be seen enjoying each other's company outdoors. The clip captures Payne lifting Cassidy into the air as the two play around together.Rather than sharing a lengthy statement, Cassidy allowed the footage and its accompanying words to convey the significance of the memory. “Treasure every moment with the people you love,” she wrote over the video. She continued, “Forever grateful this was our last hour, our last video, our last moment together. Until the next life, I’ll see you again one day.”The message reflected the importance of an ordinary moment that had become a lasting memory. What once appeared to be a lighthearted interaction between a couple now represented a time Cassidy could revisit through photographs and videos. She captioned the post simply, “2 years” alongside a red heart emoji, marking the anniversary without adding a lengthy explanation.Kate Cassidy’s heartfelt message about two years of memoriesCassidy also shared photographs of Payne on her Instagram Stories. One image carried another emotional message from the influencer, highlighting how memories continue to connect her to the singer. “2 years gone without you here but an eternity of memories. My handsome boy, I love you!!!” she wrote over the photograph.Her words showed what the anniversary means to her, as Cassidy spoke of the absence she still feels and the memories she holds on to. Her tribute was about the moments they shared, not the circumstances of Payne’s passing. By going back to a video of the two of them laughing and playing together, she gave followers a personal reminder of the relationship behind all the public attention on the singer.The posts also showed how social media can become a place where people keep the memories of loved ones close. For Cassidy, sharing the footage allowed a private moment from their relationship to become part of a public remembrance.Kate Cassidy and Liam Payne's relationshipCassidy and Payne began dating in 2022 and shared a relationship that occasionally appeared on social media. The couple travelled together and spent time away from the spotlight, giving us glimpses of their life beyond Payne’s music career. Payne rose to international fame as a member of One Direction, alongside Harry Styles, Niall Horan, Louis Tomlinson and Zayn Malik. After One Direction went on hiatus, Payne went solo, releasing music including the single ‘Strip That Down’. His personal life, meanwhile, kept drawing public interest, especially his relationship with Cassidy.In April 2025, Cassidy also talked about their final time together on Jay Shetty’s On Purpose podcast. She reflected on the emotions around their last conversation and how hard it has been to process what followed. Her latest tribute, though, went back to a simpler memory: the two of them together, laughing and enjoying each other’s company.A tribute built around remembering the little thingsKate Cassidy’s anniversary posts were a reminder that the memories that matter most are often found in everyday moments rather than grand occasions. The video she chose captured a spontaneous, affectionate moment, and her words were a reminder of how much it matters to appreciate the time we have with the people closest to us.In sharing it, Cassidy chose to remember Payne through the moments they shared together. Her message about treasuring time with loved ones made the tribute mean more, and it’ll hit home for anyone who has looked back on a memory and wished they could have it again.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Los cocineros coinciden: “Para que la salsa de tomate quede perfecta, no agregues azúcar, mejor usa un poco de bicarbonato”
articles.standfirst: Una pizca basta para neutralizar la acidez del tomate sin endulzar la receta
articles.summary: Una pizca basta para neutralizar la acidez del tomate sin endulzar la receta
articles.body: Pocas preparaciones son tan habituales en la cocina como la salsa de tomate. Acompaña pastas, pizzas, guisos y albóndigas, y casi cada casa tiene su propia receta. Sin embargo, hay un problema que se repite en muchas ollas: ese punto ácido que deja un regusto agrio y, a veces, hasta sienta mal. Para corregirlo, la costumbre más extendida es añadir una cucharadita de azúcar. Pero cada vez más cocineros advierten de que ese gesto no resuelve nada. Chefs como la italiana Roberta o el divulgador Heinz Wuth, del canal Ciencia y Cocina, explican que el azúcar solo consigue que la salsa parezca menos ácida, mientras que los ácidos del tomate siguen ahí. Wuth añade que muchos cocineros buscan rebajar la acidez para que el plato no siente mal, algo que el azúcar no logra. La alternativa que recomiendan es el bicarbonato de sodio. Al tratarse de una sustancia alcalina, reacciona con los ácidos naturales del tomate y los neutraliza. Es decir, no tapa el problema, sino que actúa directamente sobre su causa y consigue una salsa más suave sin convertirla en una preparación dulce. La clave está en la cantidad. Wuth propone entre uno y uno y medio gramos por litro de salsa, mientras que el chef Jordi Cruz habla de un gramo por cada medio kilo de sofrito. Conviene añadirlo hacia el final de la cocción y removiendo bien. Es normal que la salsa haga algo de espuma durante unos segundos: es la señal de que el bicarbonato está reaccionando. Después, hay que probar y repetir solo si sigue resultando demasiado ácida. Pasarse puede arruinar el resultado. Wuth comprobó que, con una dosis excesiva, la salsa quedaba casi neutra, perdía prácticamente todo su sabor a tomate y adquiría un ligero toque amargo. Tampoco convenció a los catadores de America’s Test Kitchen, que obtuvieron una salsa menos ácida pero de sabor plano. Además, quienes vigilan su consumo de sal deben recordar que el bicarbonato también aporta sodio. Si se prefiere no usarlo, hay otras opciones. Roberta aconseja dejar cocer el tomate al menos entre 20 y 25 minutos, aunque Wuth discute que el tiempo de cocción reduzca la acidez. Lo que sí ayuda es elegir tomates maduros y de calidad. También funcionan los ingredientes con dulzor propio, como la cebolla pochada o la zanahoria rallada, que equilibran la salsa sin necesidad de recurrir al azúcar. Así, se conserva intacto todo el sabor original del tomate.

articles.summary: Un hombre con el rostro cubierto hizo el gesto de cortar de degollar mientras la corresponsal informaba de los disturbios
articles.body: Cubrir unas protestas desde primera línea siempre implica riesgos, pero lo vivido este sábado en París demuestra hasta qué punto la tensión de la calle puede alcanzar a quienes intentan contarla. Las imágenes, grabadas durante una conexión en directo de RTVE, se han convertido en uno de los momentos más comentados de la jornada. La protagonista involuntaria es Mavi Doñate, corresponsal de la cadena pública en Francia, que informaba con casco y micrófono en mano de los disturbios que sacudían la capital. En plena intervención, un grupo de manifestantes se acercó al equipo con gritos y abucheos. Uno de ellos, vestido de negro y con el rostro cubierto, se colocó detrás de la periodista y dirigió varios gestos a la cámara, entre ellos el de cortarse el cuello. Doñate continuó con su trabajo de informar sobre todo lo que acontecía en las calles de París durante la revuelta, hasta que la conexión tuvo que interrumpirse. “Es difícil hacer la conexión”, confesó la periodista. El vídeo, difundido en redes sociales, se ha viralizado en cuestión de horas y ha sido recogido por medios de España y Latinoamérica, que destacan el carácter intimidatorio de la escena. El episodio se produjo en una de las jornadas más duras de la oleada de protestas que vive Francia. Cientos de miles de personas salieron a la calle contra la falta de profesores y el encarecimiento de la vida, y la tarde terminó con incendios, saqueos y unos 1.200 detenidos en todo el país. Doñate no fue la única periodista que sufrió la tensión. La cadena Euronews denunció que varios encapuchados atacaron a su equipo mientras grababa saqueos cerca de la plaza de la República, en el centro de París. La corresponsal de RTVE conoce bien las coberturas complicadas. Zaragozana, ocupa la corresponsalía de París desde 2021, después de seis años en Pekín, donde siguió de cerca la epidemia de coronavirus. Su trabajo le ha valido, entre otros, el Premio Ondas, el Cirilo Rodríguez y el Chaves Nogales. Mientras tanto, las protestas en Francia no dan señales de remitir y ya hay nuevas convocatorias anunciadas.

articles.title: Margate hotel festival held to give artists 'space and voice'
articles.summary: The festival has grown out of a series of smaller events held at the hotel over the past four years.
articles.body:
A week-long arts festival showcasing creative talent from across Thanet is taking place in the 110-year-old ballroom of the Walpole Bay Hotel in Margate.

Island Arts Festival , which runs until 24 October, features paintings, books, music, talks and performances by artists, writers and musicians living and working in Thanet.

Organisers said the free festival grew out of a series of smaller author and artist events held at the hotel over the past four years, expanding into a wider celebration of Thanet's creative community.

Hotel owner Jane Bishop said it gave local artists "a space and a voice".

Events planned during the week include a writers' seminar, a children's storytelling session, readings from the works of Charles Dickens, a pottery and ceramics class, talks on health through singing and an open mic session for musicians.

Festival organiser Richard Savin said the event developed from a series of annual author and artist gatherings held at the hotel and had grown "organically" into an annual arts festival in Margate's Cliftonville area, showcasing artists working and living on the Isle of Thanet.

He said he hoped the festival would make a "modest addition" to the area's arts community by encouraging interest in literature, music, painting, poetry and performance art.

Bishop said the earlier events "grew wings" and developed into a week-long arts festival.

She said her "Napery Gallery" is also on display, featuring napkins that have been turned into artworks by guests who have stayed at the hotel.

They include two by Tracey Emin, who lives and works in Margate, and has championed her hometown and formed a creative community there, the hotel owner added.

articles.title: William Shatner finds answer to 'What the f--- is heavy metal?' after forming new band at 95
articles.summary: William Shatner, 95, reveals his upcoming heavy metal album "What the F is Heavy Metal" features Queen's Brian May and over 50 musicians joining the project.
articles.body: William Shatner is showing no signs of slowing down as he prepares to front a heavy metal band at age 95. In addition to his decades-long career as an actor, Shatner is also an accomplished musician, who has released 11 studio albums encompassing a wide range of genres including spoken word, rock, progressive rock, Christmas and country releases. During an interview with Fox News Digital, Shatner, who recently partnered with over-the-counter hearing aid maker Audien Hearing for a new campaign, shared his reaction when his music label Cleopatra Records first approached him earlier this year about making a heavy metal album. WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE' "I said, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal?’" the "Star Trek" icon recalled. "And that's the title of the album, ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner added. COUNTRY MUSIC SINGER SHANE SMITH PUTS HIS OWN SPIN ON JOHNNY CASH'S ICONIC 'HURT' COVER Shatner told Fox News Digital that he teamed up with his longtime creative collaborator and friend, author Robert Sharenow, for the project. The two previously worked together on five albums featuring autobiographical lyrics and spoken-word performances. "So we wrote six songs for the album," Shatner said. "And I laid down my track." WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER, 95, ANSWERS ‘WHAT THE F--- IS HEAVY METAL?' WITH NEW ALBUM In addition to six original songs, Shatner said that "What the F is Heavy Metal" will feature covers with contributions from more than 50 musicians, "We've got one number in the album that's gonna be out in the wintertime called ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner said. "All of a sudden, 50, I'm told 50 heavy metal musicians all volunteer to be on this album." PAUL MCCARTNEY REVEALS HOW A 'HAPPY' TEEN HITCHHIKING TRIP WITH GEORGE HARRISON DELIVERED A SHOCK The musicians included Queen's Brian May, who performed a guitar solo for one of the album's tracks titled "Rage." Shatner explained that "Rage" features the famous line "Rage, rage against the dying of the light" from the 1951 poem "Do not go gentle into that good night," written by Welsh poet Dylan Thomas. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Shatner recalled that he was later invited to perform at Riot Fest, an annual three-day punk rock music festival held at Douglass Park in Chicago, Illinois. In a July social media post, the organizers of Riot Fest announced that Shatner would debut his heavy metal band The *uckers at the festival, noting that they had tried to book him for over a decade. ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES The "Boston Legal" alum said that his label tapped five musicians to form his new heavy metal band. The all-star rock and heavy metal lineup includes guitarists Marcus Nand and Britt Lightning, bassist Phil Soussan and drummer Fred Aching. "They put together a group of fabulous musicians," Shatner said. "We call ourselves The *uckers for, you know, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal.’'" BRET MICHAELS CANCELS REMAINING 2026 TOUR DATES HOURS AFTER 'COMEBACK' PERFORMANCE DUE TO HEALTH SCARE The band made its live debut in Chicago on Sept. 19 and performed at Riot Fest the following day. The *uckers played original songs including "Rage," "Sky" and "One Fear" alongside covers of Ozzy Osbourne's "Crazy Train," Motörhead's "Ace of Spades," and Metallica's "Enter Sandman." "We went to Riot Fest … and was a huge success, huge," Shatner recalled. "They were cheering and the reviews and the people…so it proved to me the viability of ‘What the F is Heavy Metal.'" ‘A MAN WITHOUT LOVE’ SINGER ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK CREDITS UNDERWATER WORKOUT FOR KEEPING HIM ‘ALIVE’ AT 90 After performing with The *uckers and making his heavy metal album, Shatner said he has an answer to his original question. "It is the beat of life," he said. "It is such an energetic way of doing music. It enlivens your life. It stirs you up. It makes you pay attention." WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HEAVY METAL ‘ENLIVENS’ HIS LIFE AS HE FRONTS BAND AT 95 Shatner explained that his approach to heavy metal extends beyond the music itself. For the album, he said he incorporated fresh takes on the lyrics of several classic songs, including Metallica’s "Enter Sandman," which he believes contains darker themes beneath its familiar melody. "I've reinterpreted even the cover songs," he said. Shatner said his version of "Enter Sandman" focuses on the sinister implications of the song’s lyrics rather than treating the Sandman as a harmless bedtime figure. "It's a total reinterpretation of the Sandman," he said. "It is amazing." While Shatner is embracing the volume of heavy metal, the project also connects to a more personal issue. The actor is partnering with Audien Hearing on a campaign about hearing health after experiencing tinnitus and hearing loss himself. Shatner recalled that his hearing challenges began decades ago on the set of "Star Trek." During the filming of an explosion scene featuring him alongside his co-star Leonard Nimoy, the stage doors were accidentally left closed, preventing the blast from dissipating properly. He told Fox News Digital that the two actors were taken to a doctor after their ears began ringing. Shatner said that he did not immediately realize that the noise had become permanent. The Canada native recalled that while walking on the beach one day, he noticed that the hiss of the retreating waves never completely disappeared. "I heard the hiss, but the hiss never went away," he said. "It was always hissing." Shatner said he eventually learned to live with the tinnitus through a process known as habituation. He also estimated that he has lost roughly 20% to 30% of his hearing and said hearing aids have helped him rediscover everyday sounds. "The dog claws on the floor, the creak of this rocking chair — all the panoply of sounds that go to make up the richness of the world around us, we’re using hearing," he said. Shatner's hearing challenges have not stopped him from playing heavy metal. However, he said the loud music can temporarily intensify the tinnitus, which he noticed after performing at Riot Fest. "Now I'm fitted with earphones, right? And the sound would have been blasting in anyway, but it's heavy metal sound," he said. "I'm blasting in on my tinnitus." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "So there is this noise," Shatner continued. "Either I'm going to perform with the noise or I'm not going to perform." "And my tinnitus is just coming back down now," he added. "It was hissing so loudly being subjected to that sound." WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE PERFORMED THROUGH ‘LOUD’ TINNITUS DURING HEAVY-METAL DEBUT AT 95 Despite the challenges that come with performing through tinnitus, Shatner said he is moving ahead with the album. He told Fox News Digital that the tracks have already been recorded, but he plans to listen to the completed music and determine whether he needs to make any changes to his performance. "So that's what's going to happen." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This is going to be a major thing in heavy metal," he added.
