articles.title: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded messages for his kids as cancer threatened to take his tongue
articles.summary: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded goodbye messages for his young children after doctors discussed removing his tongue to fight throat cancer.
articles.body: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett was staring down a terrifying possibility as he battled cancer: Doctors might have to remove his tongue. After chemotherapy and radiation failed to stop the disease, the rocker began recording messages for his young children so they could remember the sound of his voice. "I was recording pieces of information for my kids so they could watch it, because the next step was to cut my tongue out if they had to," Rockett (born Richard Allan Ream) told Fox News Digital. "And I wanted them to know what I sounded like and my advice to them growing up, and I wanted them to hear it from me. I wanted them to understand what I was, what I thought I was or would become." HOW THE NELSON TWINS WENT FROM PACKING ARENAS TO BEING 'F---ING BROKE' DESPITE MAKING MILLIONS Rockett, whose weight dropped to 161 pounds during treatment, said the possibility of losing his tongue left him fearing he might not survive much longer. "I would've most likely had a feeding tube," he said. "I don't think I would've lived much longer. It would've added another year or two. Some people do make it. Some people get all of that done and live for a long time. But I think a lot of times, with the way it was going with me, I don't think I would've survived, quite honestly." Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links. Now 65, Rockett says he has been free of cancer for a decade. His memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison," chronicles his rise to stardom during the decadent '80s and his grueling health battle. WATCH: POISON DRUMMER RIKKI ROCKETT RECALLS HEARTBREAKING CANCER BATTLE In 2015, Rockett said he and his family developed sore throats. They were all prescribed antibiotics, but while everyone else recovered, his symptoms persisted. Rockett returned to the doctor, who examined his nose and throat with a scope. During the examination, the doctor spotted something suspicious. "I don't know if it's cancer, but it's suspicious, and we got to do a biopsy," Rockett recalled his doctor telling him. "My life changed at that very second." According to the Head and Neck Cancer Alliance, Rockett was diagnosed with HPV-related throat cancer in 2015. The disease affected the base of his tongue. According to his memoir, Rockett had experienced a sore throat and a swollen lymph node for more than a month. It hurt every time he swallowed. After doctors diagnosed him with cancer, he received radiation and chemotherapy. "Before long, I couldn't eat solid food anymore," he wrote. "My weight dropped dramatically because all I could manage was soup, shakes and water. Eventually, I couldn't eat or drink anything at all." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Rockett wrote: "I've got throat cancer. At its worst, I struggle to swallow even a gulp of water. This morning, my son had to watch tears running down my cheeks as I tried to eat a spoonful of soup. He looked terrified." Rockett told Fox News Digital that he eventually "wound up in stage 4." For three months, he received radiation five days a week, along with chemotherapy weekly, but he said the treatment failed. Doctors then discussed removing his tongue, according to Rockett. Rockett was terrified. In his memoir, he wrote that he believed he had only a "40 or 50 percent chance of living." But he refused to give up. "Even with all the treatment, it still didn't work," he recalled. "So then I got on an experimental drug combination at UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center, and it worked incredibly well. It's one of those things where, if it works, it's amazing. If it doesn't, you kind of go, 'Wow, maybe I wasted my time.' So I had to roll the dice. And I did. And when I rolled it, thankfully, it came out in my favor." According to UC San Diego Health, Rockett participated in a clinical trial involving a combination of two drugs: pembrolizumab (Keytruda) and epacadostat. Rockett was declared free of throat cancer in July 2016. The treatment took a toll. At one point, Rockett's tongue swelled so much that he feared he might choke. Soon, however, a scan offered hope. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "The crazy thing was that my first PET scan showed that 90 percent of the cancer was already gone," Rockett wrote. "And by the second PET scan, it was all gone. It was as if the angels had come down and blessed me. I mean, it was unbelievable." Rockett wrote that his doctor seemed just as surprised by the results but explained that treatment needed to continue to reduce the risk of the cancer returning. But Rockett's health challenges were far from over. "Some eight months into the process, nothing was coming up, but I was getting high white blood cell counts," Rockett wrote. "So, they got concerned about that, and to cut a long story short, I wound up with something called CML, chronic myeloid leukemia, and it’s a predisposition thing. It’s a translocation between BCR-ABL, the chromosomes. You’re prone to it if, like me, you have the Philadelphia chromosome. Of course, it absolutely freaked me out. I mean, I just went through one cancer, and now I was facing another one." Chronic myeloid leukemia is a type of blood cancer often associated with an acquired genetic abnormality known as the Philadelphia chromosome. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "The hematologist, however, took everything in stride, and when we met, she was super calm," he wrote. "She told me, ‘You picked the best leukemia you could. It’s very treatable, and sometimes curable.’ Dr. Jaimeson would be my doctor for the very long foreseeable future, and I was blessed to have her." "So, all that happened was that she put me on new medication, which I’m still on. It has some nasty side effects, but the best side effect is that CML has been 100 percent in remission! Zero detection for a number of years now! There must be a reason why I’m still here, I think to this day." Looking back, Rockett told Fox News Digital his medical team "actually saved my life." Rockett still lives with the lasting effects of his treatment. But a decade after his throat cancer battle, he's focused less on what the disease took from him and more on what he lived to see — his children growing up. "Sometimes my voice gets rough, or I get dry," he said. "I get very dry because my salivary glands got toasted with the radiation. But I’m cancer-free, and I’ve been cancer free for 10 years." Rockett has no plans to slow down. He's been keeping busy performing with his band, Rockett Mafia. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I’m not out of gas yet," he said with a smile. "I still got stuff to do. And I love playing because I want my kids to see me, and they have. They’ve been to some Poison concerts. I wanted them to see me, and they did. I got that wish." For Rockett, beating cancer meant getting the time he once feared he wouldn’t have. And he's not wasting a single second, he insisted. "A big part of it was fighting for my kids," he reflected. "There’s no question that was a big chunk of my fight."

articles.title: J Mascis has nothing better to do
articles.summary: Dinosaur Jr.’s frontman, J Mascis, finally addresses the AI video for ‘Old Friends.’
articles.body: Dinosaur Jr. frontman J Mascis is known as something of a slacker guitar god. He stands stoically onstage, barely moving, as he seemingly effortlessly works through deft guitar solos and lopsided riffs. Unfortunately, Mascis has developed a similar reputation as an interview subject, quietly sitting and offering deft nonanswers. That’s not to say that Mascis can’t be funny or charming. As our interview was winding down and I was thanking him for his time, he started to loosen up a bit. He told me about his youth as a mini golf “enthusiast.” “I had a 3-foot putt for the win” at a mini-golf tournament, he said, but “that’s when I realized that I was a choker … When I was 11, I choked.” And that’s when he decided, “I should maybe not do sports.” So, instead of becoming a professional mini golfer, Mascis went on to form one of the most important bands in alternative rock. While most of his contemporaries have called it quits or are just going through the motions onstage for a paycheck, the original lineup of Mascis, bassist Lou Barlow, and drummer Patrick Murphy are still regularly putting out new LPs of reliable rockers. But Mascis says there isn’t any grand secret to the band’s longevity. Over 40 years deep, he says, “I guess we have nothing better to do.” What, for an interviewer, can come off as frustrating indifference might actually be the key to Mascis’ staying power — for better or worse. Creatively and professionally, his modus operandi seems to be rolling with the punches and not overthinking things. For the new record There Near, he said, the band “just didn’t push it.” There were no eight-hour marathon studio sessions. They weren’t meticulously fine-tuning basslines or trading Logic sessions back and forth remotely. Mascis would roll in with fully prepared demos and the band would immediately start recording, even as Barlow and Murph were still learning their parts, “on the off chance that it comes together quickly.” The same sort of relaxed approach also informs Mascis’ gear choices. He said, “I am kind of a tube purist guy, but it’s just also kind of inconvenient sometimes,” so he uses whatever works. That means while he mixes and masters to tape, he’s also tracking in Pro Tools. When it comes to designing signature instruments with Fender, he’s just as easygoing. “I try to, you know, do the important things that I want, but not make it too complicated … I think it’s better to keep it kind of cheap … just so people can do what they want with it.” The neck is his biggest concern, he said. “I’m a sucker for jumbo frets and, you know, if the neck is good and the frets and stuff, that’s the main thing. Most of the other stuff, you know, you can swap out if you want.” But that somewhat lackadaisical attitude has also caught him some heat. Two years ago, Mascis released a video for his solo track “Old Friends” that was made using generative AI. Speaking with The Verge, he finally publicly addressed the controversy. “Yeah, just some kid did it,” he said. “I thought it looked cool, so… Yeah, that’s dipping my toes into the... I don’t do much with videos.” He trailed off repeatedly while answering before finally admitting, “But yeah, I guess that’s a slippery slope.” Similarly, he said that while he doesn’t believe there is a place for AI in music making, we have to acknowledge that it’s here whether we like it or not, and “I guess we’re learning how to deal with it. And hopefully it won’t kill us all.” About the only thing that Mascis could muster strong feelings about was the band’s infamously loud live shows. (Dinosaur Jr.’s recent performance at the tiny Baby’s All Right is what finally convinced me to start packing earplugs.) “I noticed the audience too seems more desperate for something kind of reality-based,” he said, letting a touch of his purist heart show. “We don’t have in-ear monitors or click tracks. We have amps and you know, just, I think some people are responding to the reality of it. Like they really need something that’s not, you know, computer-generated or something.” He bemoaned the lack of amps onstage (Mascis plays in front of three full stacks, even in a 280-person-capacity club) and the reliance on high-tech front-of-house setups. “It’s very weird. Now, soundmen create the sound instead of capture the sound,” he said. Of course, his recognition of the visceral power of live music and directly connecting with an audience makes his indifference to AI all the more baffling. Dinosaur Jr. are currently touring the US behind There Near, which is out now.

articles.title: The Best-Dressed Stars at the Academy Museum Gala, Including Inde Navarrette and Taylor Swift
articles.summary: Taylor Swift in Dior, Sabrina Carpenter in Giorgio Armani Privé and Colman Domingo in custom Valentino were among the night's wow moments in style.
articles.body:
Forward-thinking style fresh from the Spring 2027 runways was mixed with archival and custom pieces among the stars who walked the red carpet at Saturday's Academy Museum Gala — and if there was a common thread throughout many of the looks, it was a wonderful ease, an effortless blend of relaxed chic that's not always present on an awards show carpet. After all, at the Academy Museum Gala, the few prizes awarded are predetermined and the pressure is off for everyone else.

That may be among the reasons this sixth-annual fundraiser attracted a formidable crowd that's all too happy to support the programs and exhibitions presented by the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg and Kate Capshaw served as the 2026 gala co-chairs, while the host committee this year includes Demi Moore, Rami Malek, Greta Lee, Teyana Taylor and Kate Hudson. Fold in the night's honorees — Charlize Theron, John Carpenter and Colman Domingo — and it's clear why this heavy-hitter guest list inspires thoughts that the night competes with November's LACMA Art+Film Gala for the title of "west coast Met Gala."

An influential guest list gathering to celebrate their industry, but instead their shared love of cinema may ultimately be the reason the evening's overall style blends the aforementioned relaxed-chic aesthetic with a splash of drama and, in many cases, an undeniable sense of fun. Each is found in the 15 looks that topped our list.

Taylor Swift often remains loyal to the A-line silhouette that works so well for her, and that was true of this Dior strapless gown in dove grey, crafted with panels of beautiful pleating below a gathered bodice and a splash of crystal beading. And why not? Mrs. Kelce is living her best life in her princess era. Swift completed the look with diamonds by Chopard, including earrings set with 32.40 carats of diamonds set in platinum.

Several guests eschewed floor-length gowns in favor of mid-calf lengths, and among the best was this design from Matthieu Blazy's Fall 2026 ready-to-wear collection for Chanel, worn by costume designer Miyako Bellizzi ( Uncut Gems , Scenes from a Marriage ). Blazy's collection this season references an unstructured 1920s silhouette, while this style's homage to the house's boucle tweed, embellished with paillettes, creates a thoroughly modern evening look.

From Daniel Roseberry's Fall 2026 haute-couture collection for Schiaparelli, this gown worn by Obsession star Inde Navarrette beautifully represents the artful whimsy that is synonymous with the French house. The ankle-length strapless gown is crafted in nude tulle accented with cascading polka dots on a tiered bubble skirt; Navarrette finished the look with a diamond necklace and earrings by Chopard.

The plunging neckline on this gown from Georges Chakra's Fall 2026/2027 couture collection thoroughly flattered Anna Kendrick, from its deep V to the sleeveless black guipure lace bodice, the flared hips above the fitted skirt, and the accents of quill paillettes. Amid a sea of black gowns Saturday night, Kendrick stood out beautifully.

Social media kicked into a frenzy when Cailee Spaeny arrived in this Valentino gown, from the Spring 2027 collection that Alessandro Michele sent down the runway on October 4. From the fuchsia silk strapless gown to its pleated train in rose and pale pink, Instagram fans instantly fell in love with the tonal mix (a black bow in back, however, divided style pundits, some deeming it an unnecessary detail).

Honored with the night's Vantage Award, presented to an artist who helps to "challenge dominant narratives around cinema," Colman Domingo was among the night's most anticipated arrivals, because it was a safe bet he would turn up in a look worthy of both the evening and his personal style. And he didn't disappoint, wearing a custom beaded jacket by Valentino, paired with a black tuxedo shirt, tuxedo trousers, and the bow tie undone around this neck, a statement of maximum cool. Domingo finished his look with jewels by Boucheron and an Omega timepiece.

Everything about this look, from Tamara Ralph's Fall 2026 couture collection, worked on Jessica Biel, from the feathers that framed her face to the bodice cut that emphasized her shoulders and that terrific high slit. Feathers were among the night's trends, and the look on Biel was equal parts fun, sleek and glamorous. She completed her look with diamond earrings and rings by Chopard.

This decidedly modern take on a tuxedo is from the feverish mind of Pierpaolo Piccioli for his Balenciaga Fall 2026 couture collection — and if anyone could carry it off, it's Rhea Seehorn, who often adopts a forward-thinking approach in her red-carpet style. Piccioli's maximalist take was inspired by the volume beloved by Cristobal Balenciaga, and Seehorn carried it off with ease. She finished her look with Englebert 1920 jewelry.

Sabrina Carpenter in Giorgio Armani Privé

Sapphire blue is a trending color for Fall 2026, so it's fitting that it would be worn by the woman who routinely sets style trends. Sabrina Carpenter's custom Giorgio Armani Privé blue silk cady gown was inspired by a look from the house's Spring/Summer 2026 collection, but the stunning element is the surprise of the superstar's back, an open design with tassels cascading from her shoulders. She completed her look with diamond and sapphire earrings by Chopard.

The star of The Diplomat wore a head-to-toe look by Dunhill, including the house's Bourdon double-breasted jacket in brown cotton velvet, paired with a formal bib point collar shirt, single-pleat trousers, and the house's Made in England Chelsea boots. Sewell finished the look with IWC's Portugieser Automatic 40 timepiece.

There was a terrific 1970s vibe about the Dior gown Mia Goth chose for the Academy Museum Gala, from its overall relaxed ease to its bias-cut sleeves and subtle sequined embellishment. The actress accessorized the dress with Dior fine jewelry and a Dior handbag.

Not unlike Seehorn's tuxedo take, the volume was plentiful in Naomi Ackie's custom Balenciaga gown, a look inspired by the Fall 2026 haute-couture collection. Crafted in aubergine taffeta, the gown featured a strapless bubble bodice, a sweeping train — and, as many pointed out on social media, pockets. The actress completed her look with diamond earrings and ring by Boucheron.

At the other end of the volume spectrum, Gemma Chan opted for the sleek minimalism of Prada, a pink silk gabardine dress with a front cutout detail and a draped back knot. Diamond jewels by Cartier, including the house's Agrafe earrings, completed Chan's look.

The glamorous wave in Kate Hudson's hair echoed the sculpted, crystal-embroidered ruffle that trailed down the opposite side of her custom Giorgio Armani Privé gown in blush pink. From the color of the gown against her skin to her '40s-inspired hair and her Harry Winston diamonds, it all worked.

articles.title: In 2022, when Johnny Depp won a defamation verdict against Amber Heard and said, 'The jury gave my life back,' here’s what happened during the six-week trial
articles.summary: In a landmark defamation trial, Johnny Depp was awarded $10.35 million after the jury ruled in his favor against Amber Heard, who was found liable for defamation. The six-week trial captivated global audiences and raised important discussions about domestic abuse and public opinion. Both parties issued statements following the verdict. Get the full details of the trial and its implications.
articles.body: Johnny Depp and Amber Heard’s case is perhaps one of the most publicized divorces in Hollywood history. In June 2022, a jury in Fairfax County, Virginia, ruled overwhelmingly in favor of Johnny Depp in his high-profile defamation lawsuit against his ex-wife, Amber Heard. The case was televised across six weeks and captivated global audiences and sparked widespread debate surrounding defamation law, public opinion, and domestic abuse allegations.What happened between Amber Heard and Johnny Depp that led to the case?Johnny Depp filed a defamation lawsuit against Amber Heard because of a 2018 opinion piece she wrote in the The Washington Post, in which she had described herself as a "public figure representing domestic abuse." While she did not specifically mention Depp in the opinion piece, Depp had presented the argument that her conversation was directly leading to the domestic abuse allegations that she had brought up during their 2016 divorce case.He made claims in the defamation lawsuit that Heard’s comments and the false implications and accusations have severely harmed his personal reputation and cost him acting roles in Hollywood, which included being dropped from major film franchises, such as the ‘Fantastic Beasts’ franchise. At the time, he had filed a defamation lawsuit of USD 50 million, to which Heard had filed a countersuit of USD 100 million, alleging that statements made by Depp’s former lawyer, Adam Waldman, who called her abuse claims, a "hoax," defamed her.More about the 6-week-long trial and verdict that followed Johnny Depp and Amber HeardThe Los Angeles Times reported at the time that the trial itself went on for 6 weeks. Though on June 1, 2022, after deliberating for roughly 12 hours across three days, the seven-person jury delivered its verdict in favor of Depp. They held Heard liable on all of the three counts of defamation, ruling that her statements were false, made with "actual malice," and intended to defame Depp. He was awarded USD 10 million in compensatory damages and an additional USD 5 million in other punitive damages. Due to Virginia state caps on punitive damages, the judge reduced that portion to USD 350,000, bringing his total to USD 10.35 million.Depp was also found liable in one of the three counts in Heard’s countersuit and was made to pay Heard USD 2 million out of the original amount of USD 100 million that the actress had filed the case under.Later on, the two made deals outside of the courtroom, and Heard agreed to pay Depp $1 million to resolve the litigation, funded entirely by her insurance provider.Johnny Depp posted about the defamation case winDepp shared an Instagram post after the official verdict was served, writing, "Speaking the truth was what I owed to my children and those who have remained steadfast in their support of me. I feel at peace knowing I have finally accomplished that.”He added, “Six years ago, my life, the life of my children, the lives of those closest to me, and also, the lives of the people who for many, many years have supported and believed in me were forever changed. All in the blink of an eye... And six years later, the jury gave me my life back. I am truly humbled.”Amber Heard’s post about the case verdictFollowing the verdict, the ‘Aquaman’ actress also issued her own statement on her social media channels. She wrote, “The disappointment I feel today is beyond words. I'm heartbroken that the mountain of evidence still was not enough to stand up to the disproportionate power, influence, and sway of my ex-husband. I'm even more disappointed with what this verdict means for other women. It is a setback. It sets back the clock to a time when a woman who spoke up and spoke out could be publicly shamed and humiliated. It sets back the idea that violence against women is to be taken seriously."On the work front, since the publicized case, Heard has been staying in Spain with her children, living away from the hustle and bustle of Hollywood. Whereas Depp has formally entered the acting market and is slated to appear in 'Ebenezer.'Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: MUMBAI: A vehicle carrying Hindi film actor Tiger Shroff, son of Jackie Shroff and Ayesha Shroff, was shot at multiple times by unidentified armed men
articles.body: MUMBAI: A vehicle carrying Hindi film actor Tiger Shroff, son of Jackie Shroff and Ayesha Shroff, was shot at multiple times by unidentified armed men near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu on Sunday evening.The actor is reportedly out of danger.As per preliminary reports, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack.A voice note and an X post purportedly from Anil Pandit claimed that anyone who works with Salman Khan would be targeted."Sooner or later, number sabka aayega," Pandit allegedly said.Tiger Shroff and his driver, identified as Firdaus, were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Hospital sources issued a preliminary assessment, saying the driver had suffered a bullet injury to his left hand. Police were yet to confirm this.Doctors said the actor had sustained a few abrasions but no bullet wounds. Police took them to the emergency room (ER) at Nanavati Hospital.The third person injured in the Tiger Shroff firing incident, Yogesh Chavan, sustained bullet injuries to his chest, Cooper Hospital doctors said.Juhu Police were investigating the crime scene. An officer said, "Tiger Shroff is safe. He has not suffered any firearm injury. Further investigation is underway."A forensic team collected evidence from the spot where the firing took place. Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the incident.The Bishnoi gang has previously used social media to claim responsibility for attacks.The incident sparked alarm in film and political circles, given the previous fatal attack on politician Baba Siddiqui in Bandra and the firing incident at Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartment in Bandra Bandstand.In July 2026, the gang last issued a threat to actor Aamir Khan.Siddiqui's son Zeeshan expressed shock and horror over Sunday's attack on Tiger Shroff, while NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule voiced concern over the worsening law and order situation in the state.Several commentators expressed concern over the safety of the common man on crowded streets, as the attack occurred around 7pm on a weekend.Tiger's mother, Ayesha Shroff, was not available for comment.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis called the Mumbai Police Commissioner to inquire about the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff. articles.summary: Tiger Shroff reportedly escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne men opened fire in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening.
articles.body: Tiger Shroff reportedly escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne men opened fire in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. The incident took place as the actor was leaving a venue in the area after playing football at Pushpa Park. According to initial reports, fans had gathered outside the venue to catch a glimpse of the actor when the firing took place. While Tiger remained safe, his driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured in the incident, police said.Video captures sounds of gunshots; Mumbai Crime Branch reaches spotAccording to the TV9 report, from the preliminary information, Tiger Shroff was travelling in his BMW when shots were fired from the crowd outside the venue. A video has also surfaced on social media in which five gunshots can reportedly be heard. Following the incident, the area was sealed off, and the Mumbai Crime Branch reached the spot to investigate. Further details about the circumstances surrounding the firing and the identities of the alleged attackers are awaited.Meanwhile, according to ANI report, Mumbai Police said, "A firing incident has been reported under Juhu Police Station. Actor Tiger Shroff is safe and has not sustained any gunshot injuries. Further investigation is underway."Ashish Shelar calls the incident unfortunate and says no culprits will be sparedMaharashtra cabinet minister Ashish Shelar addressed the incident in an interview with TV9, describing it as unfortunate and asserting that no culprits would be spared. He said that, according to the initial information he had received, Tiger and his friends had visited Juhu for a football match. Shelar also confirmed that the actor’s driver had been hospitalised at Nanavati Hospital following the incident.Minister speaks to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven BhartiShelar further said that he had spoken to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and Joint Commissioner of Police Manoj Sharma regarding the matter. According to the minister, Sharma was present at the venue as the investigation got underway. The police are expected to examine the available evidence and establish the sequence of events leading up to the firing.Lawrence Bishnoi gang reportedly claims responsibilityAccording to a TV9 report, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang has claimed responsibility for the firing incident. The claim has not been independently verified in the information available at the time of writing. The investigation is ongoing, and further details are awaited.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has claimed responsibility for the attack after gangster Anil Pandit alleged that he, along with Harman Sandhu, was behind the incident. "We had called him and tried to explain things to him, but he did not understand. So today, we made sure to explain it to him properly," the post said in Hindi. Pandit also issued a warning, stating, "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch."Tiger Shroff, 36, is the son of veteran Bollywood actor Jackie Shroff and is known for films including 'Heropanti', 'Baaghi' and 'War'. He was last seen in A Harsha's 'Baaghi 4', which also starred Sanjay Dutt, Sonam Bajwa and Harnaaz Sandhu.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Nuria Roca alucina al ver un paraguas que funciona sin mango ante la incredulidad de Juan del Val: “Pensaba que era una nave espacial”
articles.standfirst: El propio televisivo lo calificó como ”fascinante” y “estúpido” a la vez
articles.summary: El propio televisivo lo calificó como ”fascinante” y “estúpido” a la vez
articles.body: La tecnología continúa evolucionando a pasos gigantescos. En este sentido, en ‘La Roca’, programa de La Sexta que dirige y presenta Nuria Roca cada fin de semana, se trató un invento tan llamativo como sorprendente a la vez: un paraguas sin mango que funciona a modo de dron y que es manejado con un mando. Lo sacó a escena Juan del Val, que se hizo eco de un vídeo difundido sobre él en redes sociales y explicó al detalle cómo funciona y en qué consiste. Sobre ello, se pronunció su esposa Nuria Roca, que dejó una llamativa reflexión. Del Val trajo al plató un vídeo de una persona con un paraguas sin mango que se movía a dónde iba esa persona mientras llovía: “Desconozco quién lo ha creado. Me parece fascinante, revolucionario y estúpido a la vez, pero te sigue a donde tú vayas para no mojarte”. La batería dura diez minutos y todo “son ventajas”, según el colaborador, pero “no sirve para nada”. Cree que no es muy útil porque cuando andas y el paraguas te sigue sigue cayendo lluvia por los lados, haciéndose la siguiente pregunta: “¿Tanto cuesta que lleve un mango para evitarlo?”. Los colaboradores presentes en el plató de la edición de este domingo, 18 de octubre, de ‘La Roca’ reaccionaban a cada dato que daba Del Val con algunos comentarios como “¡Qué maravilla!”, “¡Qué cosa tan sorprendente”, “¡Qué guay!” o “Impresionante”. Sin embargo, Nuria Roca, cuando Juan del Val acabó la explicación sobre este paraguas, dejó la siguiente reflexión: “Hay que mejorarlo un poco. Pensaba que era una nave espacial”. A lo que sentenció Juan del Val: “Si no quieres un paraguas pues te pones un chubasquero y ya está, así evitarás mojarte y calarte”.

articles.title: Assam marks Kati Bihu with prayers
articles.summary: Assam observes Kati Bihu with prayers, earthen lamps (sakis) and rituals for healthy paddy crops; Governor Acharya and CM Himanta Biswa Sarma extend greetings.
articles.body: Guwahati: Assam marked Kati Bihu on Sunday with prayers, earthen lamps and rituals for healthy crops and a good harvest.The agrarian festival is observed in mid-Oct, when paddy crops are growing in the fields.Unlike Rongali Bihu, which marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring, and Bhogali Bihu, associated with harvest and abundance, Kati Bihu is observed through prayers and the lighting of sakis, or earthen lamps.People light sakis near Tulsi plants in their courtyards and in paddy fields, seeking blessings for healthy crops and protection from pests and insects. The lamps are also associated with prayers for family well-being and prosperity.Assam Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya and CM Himanta Biswa Sarma extended greetings to the people on the occasion.In a social media post, Acharya described Kati Bihu as an embodiment of Assam’s agrarian and cultural life and prayed for the well-being of the people.“On this sacred occasion of Kati Bihu, the embodiment of agrarian and cultural life of Assamese society, I offer my heartfelt devotion and reverence to the Almighty for the well-being of the people of the state,” he said.Sarma expressed hope that the festival would bring hope, prosperity and happiness to every household. “May Maa Lakshmi bless our farmers and Assam with a bountiful harvest,” he added.Cabinet minister Atul Bora, who took part in the observance at Mahura Pathar in Bokakhat, said, “Rooted in Assam’s agrarian traditions, Kati Bihu reflects the close relationship between the state’s cultural practices and rice cultivation. The festival symbolises hope and faith as farmers await the ripening of their crops and the arrival of the harvest season.”He added that PM Narendra Modi govt, as well as CM Himanta Biswa Sarma-led govt, has been continuously prioritising the farmers’ interests by taking various initiatives for the farmers’ welfare.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Dua Lipa fights Samsung’s bid to dismiss $15 million lawsuit over alleged unauthorised use of her photo on TV boxes, claiming the packaging falsely suggested she endorsed its products
articles.summary: Pop superstar Dua Lipa is pushing back against Samsung’s attempt to throw out her $15 million lawsuit over the alleged unauthorised use of her photograph
articles.body: Pop superstar Dua Lipa is pushing back against Samsung’s attempt to throw out her $15 million lawsuit over the alleged unauthorised use of her photograph on television packaging. The singer’s legal team argues that displaying her image on the company’s TV boxes could have led consumers to believe she had endorsed its products, turning what Samsung describes as a showcase of entertainment content into a dispute over celebrity image rights.According to Law Commentary, Lipa’s attorneys filed their response to Samsung’s motion to dismiss on October 16, 2026, in the US District Court for the Central District of California. The filing challenges the company’s arguments on false endorsement and publicity rights, while maintaining that the alleged use of her likeness requires legal scrutiny.The court has not yet ruled on Samsung’s request, and the allegations remain disputed.How Dua Lipa’s photograph landed on Samsung TV packagingAt the centre of the legal battle is a photograph of Lipa taken backstage at the 2024 Austin City Limits music festival. According to her lawsuit, the image appeared inside a simulated television screen printed on Samsung’s retail boxes, alongside content available through its Samsung TV Plus streaming service.Lipa filed the lawsuit on May 8, 2026, alleging copyright infringement, trademark infringement, false endorsement and violations of her right of publicity. She claims Samsung used the photograph on television packaging for products sold in the United States during 2025 and 2026 without her permission, despite repeated demands to stop.The singer is seeking at least $15 million in damages, in addition to further relief connected to profits she alleges the company earned through the disputed use of her image.For Lipa, the issue is not simply whether her photograph appeared on a television box. Her lawyers argue that placing a recognisable celebrity’s image on a consumer product can create the impression of a commercial partnership, particularly when that celebrity is known for carefully selected brand collaborations.Samsung denies implying that Dua Lipa endorsed its productsSamsung has challenged the singer’s interpretation of the packaging. The company maintains that the photograph was used to illustrate entertainment content available through its televisions and was not intended to suggest that Lipa personally endorsed its products.Samsung has also said a third-party content provider assured it that the necessary permissions had been obtained, including permission for use on retail packaging. The company denies intentionally misusing the singer’s likeness.In its September 10 motion to dismiss, Samsung argued that a celebrity’s face does not automatically qualify as a trademark. It also maintained that consumers would understand the photograph as an illustration of content available on a television, rather than evidence of an endorsement.Lipa’s legal team has rejected that reasoning. According to the October 16 filing, the singer selectively licenses her name and likeness through commercial partnerships, including deals with major luxury brands. Her attorneys argue that consumers familiar with those arrangements could reasonably interpret her appearance on Samsung’s packaging as another authorised brand association.The disagreement places the question of consumer perception at the centre of the false endorsement claim: whether the packaging was merely showcasing entertainment content or could have conveyed the impression that Lipa had approved or sponsored Samsung’s products.Why English law is another flashpoint in the lawsuitSamsung is also challenging the legal basis of Lipa’s publicity-right claims. The company argues that because the singer is domiciled in England, English law should apply rather than California’s statutory protections for the commercial use of a person’s identity.Samsung contends that English law does not recognise the equivalent standalone right of publicity that Lipa seeks to enforce.Her lawyers have disputed both the choice of law and Samsung’s interpretation of the protections available under English law. They argue that California law should govern the alleged commercial exploitation of her image on products marketed and sold in the state.According to Law Commentary, Lipa’s attorneys have also warned that Samsung’s interpretation could leave English celebrities with fewer avenues to challenge the unauthorised commercial use of their identities in California.The issue could prove significant in determining which of the singer’s claims can proceed. However, it is separate from the court’s assessment of her copyright, trademark and false endorsement allegations.US District Judge Christina A. Snyder has not ruled on Samsung’s motion to dismiss. The company is scheduled to submit its reply on November 13, 2026, and a hearing is set for December 14, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Rabiot and Gila ‘angry’ after Milan threaten to fumble 3-0 advantage
articles.summary: Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila were ‘angry’ after Milan’s chaotic 3-2 win over Atalanta, as they almost fumbled a 3-0 advantage. ‘I’m not so sure we deserve it...
articles.body:
Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila were 'angry' after Milan's chaotic 3-2 win over Atalanta , as they almost fumbled a 3-0 advantage. 'I'm not so sure we deserve it.'

It was a strange game at San Siro this evening, because the Rossoneri surged into a 3-0 lead and seemed perhaps too comfortable with the Goncalo Ramos penalty, Rabiot and Gila on target.

They even saw Ramos have another penalty parried by Marco Carnesecchi, but Atalanta staged a late comeback with Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic goals, only a desperate Mike Maignan save preventing 3-3.

ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Adrien Rabiot of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team's second goal with teammates during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"We did very well in the first half, then strangely we lost control of the game," Rabiot told Sky Sport Italia.

"It is a problem, because we had done so well, but if we don't keep that up, then it's not worth anything.

"Fortunately, we were able to get the victory, but I'm not so sure we deserve it. I feel quite angry, we cannot suddenly stop after playing that well and we need more from those who come off the bench."

ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, gives instructions to Adrien Rabiot during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

This was just days after Milan crushed RB Salzburg 4-0 away from home in the Europa League, with an Alphadjo Cisse hat-trick, but the teenager didn't get a look-in this evening.

Defender Gila did get his first Serie A goal since 2024, nodding in a Rabiot flick at the back post from a corner.

"We had dominated for 65 minutes, but then we tried to move the ball around too hastily, we lacked patience and lost control of the match," added Gila.

"It's a pity, because the first half was perhaps our best performance of the season."

ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Mario Gila of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

At least Milan remain unbeaten in Serie A so far this season, even if they have shown serious problems in defence.

"You need to win these games, even when you're not in great shape and don't do that well. We've got to learn from this experience."

articles.title: Gattuso wanted to quit coaching career: ‘I always had a stomachache’
articles.summary: Lazio coach Gennaro Gattuso admits he wanted to quit coaching in the first years of his career: I always had a stomachache, and I got angry, but I belong on...
articles.body:
Lazio coach Gennaro Gattuso admits he wanted to quit coaching in the first years of his career: I always had a stomachache, and I got angry, but I belong on the field.'

Gattuso spoke to DAZN ahead of Lazio's away game at Juventus.

"We play against a team that makes you struggle on the wings. They have a great coach, but it's about mentality," Gattuso said.

ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Saba Goglichidze of AC Monza scores his team's first goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and AC Monza at Stadio Olimpico on October 11, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

"We can't manage the game; if we have to lose, we lose our way. We need to play to reference points and have courage, but sometimes we lack both.

"We want to start strong from minute one. We need courage; sometimes we might defend with a low block, but when we press with strikers, we must be aggressive," he added.

"I know we might struggle against Kolo Muani's pace, or McKennie playing as an attacking midfielder or on the wing, but we're here to play it."

VENICE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 19: SS Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on September 19, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

Gattuso is in his first season at Lazio as the Biancocelesti hired him last summer, months after he failed to bring Italy to the 2026 World Cup.

The Biancocelesti have grabbed 16 points in the opening six Serie A games of the season.

"I must say that experiences abroad have helped me. We must change the players. If we want to do this job, we must get into the players' heads," Gattuso said.

VENICE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 19: Head coach of SS Lazio Gennaro Gattuso looks on during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on September 19, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images)

"There are two or three things that are not negotiable. In the first years, I wanted to quit. When I got home, I always had a stomachache, and I got angry. I had to think differently. I tried to stay home, but honestly I missed football too much, so after two or three months, I got annoyed and started bothering the people close to me. I belong in the field; I like it. Even when the results weren't there and I struggled. My decisions prove it.

"I came here for one reason. Last season, they proved they could play in a certain way. I had already coached three or four of these players, so it was an easy choice. Hopefully, they'll continue."

articles.title: Mister Organ is one of the most unsettling documentaries I’ve ever seen
articles.summary: The story of Michael Organ is the rare documentary that doubles as a psychological horror film.
articles.body: Mister Organ doesn’t reach the level of societal horror of The Act of Killing or the creepypasta-meets-true-crime gruesomeness of Beware the Slenderman, but there’s something deeply unsettling about Michael Organ and his intimate campaign of terror against everyone who enters his life. Mister Organ is a documentary by David Farrier, an Auckland, New Zealand journalist. The movie starts with Farrier reporting on Bashford Antiques, a shop in Ponsonby that has begun aggressively clamping cars in its lot and demanding exorbitant fees to release them — up to $760. Farrier’s article for The Spinoff eventually led the government to introduce legislation that would outlaw extreme clamping fees. Under normal circumstances, that would be the end of the story. But at the center of this story is a man named Michael Organ who turns out to be a bizarre, seemingly dangerous conman. [Media: Organ was hired to police Bashford’s lot, and during his investigation, Farrier discovers he’s more than just a parking-lot bully. Years earlier, Organ had been charged with attempting to steal a yacht in an elaborate scheme. What’s more, he claimed to be a prince and a lawyer — he is neither. As Farrier talks to people who have known Organ and interacts with him directly, what emerges is a portrait of a deeply troubled man who has left a trail of traumatized people in his wake. The movie shifts from a wild portrait of a conman to something more alarming and tense when Organ reveals he’s gotten his hands on a key to Farrier’s home and only warns him to be careful. From there it spirals even further; eventually, Farrier felt it necessary to leave the country to protect himself from Organ’s campaign of harassment and gaslighting. It’s the rare documentary that doubles as a psychological horror film. Mister Organ is available to stream on Hoopla, Kanopy, and YouTube.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford mourns son Presley Gerber in heartbreaking tribute
articles.summary: Cindy Crawford called Presley Gerber a "sweet, beautiful soul" in an emotional Instagram tribute weeks after his death at a rehabilitation facility.
articles.body: Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber are remembering their late son and brother, Presley Walker Gerber, as a "sweet, beautiful soul" in heartbreaking tributes shared weeks after his death. "Presley Walker Gerber. July 2, 1999—September 20, 2026," Crawford wrote on Instagram, alongside a photo of her son. "We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years," she continued. "He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever." Crawford praised Presley for "how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability" and thanked the public for supporting the family since the devastating loss. GEORGE CLOONEY SAYS FAMILY IS STILL PROCESSING PRESLEY GERBER'S TRAGIC DEATH "We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," the model wrote. "Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia." PRESLEY GERBER DEAD AT 27: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT CINDY CRAWFORD, RANDE GERBER'S FAMILY Kaia, Presley’s younger sister, shared her own tribute on Instagram, describing her brother as her "ultimate teacher," "best buddy" and "great protector." CHAD LOWE’S DAUGHTER MABEL SHARES HEARTBREAKING TRIBUTE TO LATE SISTER FIONA, 13 "I don’t have the words," Kaia wrote. "And maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth." "You know how much i loved being your sister: it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole." "you believed — always believed — in people. you met cruelty not with anger, but with confusion. and curiosity. you believed people were inherently good because, presley, you are inherently good." Kaia recalled being scared to get her ears pierced when the two were younger. "i got scared before getting my ears pierced, so you went first. you always went first. but when i held the earring they took from your body, all i could think was: that belongs to you." "and i really f—ing wish you hadn’t gone first this time." In another passage, Kaia said she was still learning how to be Presley’s sister "in a world that I can’t reach for you in." "I don’t know how to do that yet," she wrote. She ended the tribute with a series of heartbreaking declarations. "My darling brother. I do adore you," Kaia wrote. "I love my brother. My brother is dead." "And this party sucks so bad without you, prez," she added. Gerber died Sept. 20 at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. PRESLEY GERBER’S FINAL HOURS AT REHAB IN FOCUS AMID CAUSE OF DEATH QUESTIONS The model's cause of death was "deferred," according to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The medical examiner told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available." PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department. A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time." GEORGE CLOONEY RUSHES TO RANDE GERBER AND CINDY CRAWFORD'S SIDE AFTER SON PRESLEY'S DEATH Months before his death, Presley Gerber shared a raw look at his battle with addiction and the treatment he hoped would help him find his way back to himself. In March, the model posted a video of himself preparing to undergo an "ibogaine flood dose," a psychedelic treatment, at a wellness clinic in Cancún, Mexico. According to Stanford Medicine, ibogaine is a naturally occurring psychedelic derived from the root bark of the Tabernanthe iboga shrub. It has "gained interest from the medical and scientific communities for its potential to treat opioid and cocaine addiction, and research has suggested that it increases signaling of several important molecules within the brain, some of which have been linked to drug addiction and depression." The treatment is legal in some countries, but not in the United States. "Quiet moment before everything changed," Presley Gerber wrote in the Instagram caption. "I was absolutely terrified, and I knew I would be again if I ever had to face something like this." Gerber said letting go of control was difficult, but he trusted "there was something bigger than me guiding it." CARA DELEVINGNE ADMITS SHE USED PARTY DRUG GHB DAILY BEFORE TERRIFYING SEIZURES FORCED HER SOBER "I knew why I was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself," he wrote. He also said he was "praying it’s the last time" he would need to return for treatment. Presley Gerber’s post was one of several instances in which he publicly documented his recovery journey. In recent years, he had spoken candidly about depression, panic attacks, addiction and the challenges of seeking treatment. During a 2023 episode of the "Studio 22" podcast, Presley Gerber discussed his experiences with depression and other mental health challenges. "[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It’s a 24/7 job, and there’s so much to it," he said. "That’s really what I want to do is help people, whether you’re depressed, you’re struggling with something that is having a negative effect on your body," he continued. "I mean it could be anything, and there’s no judgment." Gerber said he hoped his experiences could help other people avoid making similar mistakes. "I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things," he said. "What I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people, so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made." He also explained why he wanted to be open about his mental health journey. articles.title: Disha Patani visits Tiger Shroff’s residence after firing incident; Eknath Shinde meets family, condemns attack; Devendra Fadnavis calls actor, assures swift action
articles.summary: Disha Patani, along with Krishna Shroff, visited Tiger Shroff’s residence following the firing incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area, as Maharashtra Deputy Chief
articles.body: Disha Patani, along with Krishna Shroff, visited Tiger Shroff’s residence following the firing incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area, as Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde also visited the actor’s home and Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis called him to offer support. The developments came hours after Shroff narrowly escaped an attack in which unidentified men allegedly opened fire at his car, leaving two people injured.Patani, who shares a close friendship with Tiger and his family, was seen arriving at his residence after the incident. The visits and calls from senior political leaders came amid heightened concern over the safety of Bollywood personalities following the shooting.Tiger was unharmed in the incident, while his driver sustained a gunshot injury. Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to track down those responsible, and the investigation is underway.Jackie Shroff confirms son Tiger is safeThe attack has also prompted reactions from several Bollywood personalities, with actors and filmmakers expressing shock and concern. Ranvir Shorey, filmmaker Rahul Dholakia and Poonam Pandey were among those who reacted to the incident, raising concerns about law and order and the safety of people in Mumbai.Tiger’s father, actor Jackie Shroff, later confirmed to media persons that his son was safe.Eknath Shinde visits Tiger Shroff’s residence, condemns attackMaharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde strongly condemned the firing incident and stressed that the safety of celebrities and ordinary citizens remained the government’s priority.Speaking to the media, Shinde described the attack on Tiger’s vehicle as deeply concerning and said he had spoken to the Mumbai Police Commissioner. He also said the commissioner had formed several teams to identify and apprehend those responsible.“Our current priority is to keep Mumbai and its citizens safe. Whether it is a celebrity or an ordinary citizen, ensuring their safety is the responsibility of both the police and the government. There will be no laxity in this regard, and no gang, whoever they may be, will be spared,” Shinde said.Referring to Mumbai’s history of gang wars in the 1990s, the Deputy Chief Minister warned against attempts to spread fear in the city. He said the police would take action to maintain law and order and ensure those responsible were brought to justice.Devendra Fadnavis calls Tiger Shroff, assures swift actionMaharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also spoke to Tiger Shroff following the incident and assured him that the accused would be traced and apprehended at the earliest.“We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest,” Fadnavis told the actor.According to sources in the Chief Minister’s Office, Fadnavis had earlier contacted the Mumbai Police Commissioner to seek details of the firing. He directed the commissioner to ensure a swift investigation and strict action against those responsible.The government’s response came as police intensified their investigation into the shooting, which took place in the Juhu area on Sunday.Tiger Shroff escapes unharmed as driver suffers gunshot injuryAccording to Mumbai Police, three to four rounds were fired at Tiger’s car as he was leaving a ground after football practice. A large crowd had gathered to see the actor, and police said shots were fired at his vehicle from within the crowd.Tiger was not hit by any bullets. His driver, identified in police updates as Firdosh, sustained a gunshot wound to his left arm and was taken to Nanavati Hospital for treatment. Another person, identified as Mr Chauhan in an earlier police statement, was also injured and was undergoing treatment. An autorickshaw driver was among those reported to have been hurt in the incident.Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg said police teams had been deployed and a forensic team had examined the scene to collect evidence. The incident falls under the jurisdiction of Juhu Police Station, and further investigation is underway.The firing triggered panic in the area, with people reportedly running for cover after hearing the gunshots. Police cordoned off the scene as investigators began examining the circumstances surrounding the attack.Unverified gang claim surfaces after shootingAfter the incident, a video circulated on social media in which a man identifying himself as Anil Pandit and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang took responsibility for the firing. The man allegedly described the attack as a warning to Tiger to stop working with Salman Khan.However, police had not officially confirmed the gang’s involvement in the shooting in the information available at the time of reporting. The claim circulating online remains unverified.The allegation has drawn attention because of the reported hostility between members of the Bishnoi gang and Salman Khan, linked to the actor’s alleged involvement in the 1998 blackbuck poaching case in Rajasthan. The Bishnoi community reveres the blackbuck.The gang has also been linked by investigators to previous attacks involving people associated with Khan. The 2024 killing of former Maharashtra legislator Baba Siddique in Bandra East, which was claimed by the Bishnoi gang, had further raised concerns about organised crime and threats connected to the film industry.For now, the motive behind the firing at Tiger Shroff’s car and the identity of those responsible remain subjects of the police investigation.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia."Cindy Crawford remembers son Presley GerberKaia Gerber pays touching tribute to brother Presley GerberRande and daughter, Kaia, also broke their silence and paid touching tribute to Presley. Kaia, posting a throwback video from their childhood, wrote, "I don't have the words. and maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn't need them all along. words fail and words subtract and words summarise, and words lack truth. and how naive of me to believe that language could transcend grief."She went on to write, "I am quite literally down on my f*****g knees. you know how much i loved being your sister. it has always been and will forever be, my favourite thing about myself. I came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. I had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i'm certain its going to swallow me whole."Recalling their time together and the final moments as brother and sister, she said, "I keep thinking about how when we were little, i got scared before getting my ears pierced so you went first. you always went first. but when i held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: that belongs to you. and i really fucking wish you hadn't gone first this time."In a tear-jerking conclusion, she added, "you missed our date. i forgive you. keep a place for me in the meantime. because, presley, even knowing where it ends, i would choose it all over again. every second. i would walk knowingly toward this grief if it meant that on the other side of it i got to be your sister."Rande Gerber on son Presley Gerber's passingRande later posted the same tribute on his own page, and he also reshared daughter Kaia's post, writing alongside a red heart emoji, "My life, my world, my heart. A moment that will live in me forever."Investigation into Presley’s death remains ongoing. articles.title: Tiger Shroff car firing: FWICE condemns firing incident, seeks immediate security for actor and family
articles.summary: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) on Sunday strongly condemned the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's vehicle
articles.body: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) on Sunday strongly condemned the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's vehicle and called for immediate security measures to ensure the safety of the actor and his family.FWICE condemns firing at Tiger ShroffIn a press release, FWICE stated that acts of violence and intimidation were unacceptable and raised serious concerns about the safety and security of personalities associated with the Indian film industry."It is deeply disturbing that this is the second such incident involving a prominent personality from the film industry, following the earlier firing incident involving renowned filmmaker Rohit Shetty. The recurrence of such incidents is a matter of grave concern and calls for immediate, decisive and effective action by the concerned authorities," the statement read.FWICE demands investigation into shootingFWICE demanded a thorough, impartial and time-bound investigation into the incident involving Tiger Shroff to ensure that those responsible are identified and brought to justice."We appeal to the Government of Maharashtra and the concerned police authorities to take serious cognisance of these repeated attacks and implement effective measures to ensure a safer and more secure environment for all personalities associated with the film industry. FWICE places its full trust and faith in the Mumbai Police and has equal confidence in the Chief Minister of Maharashtra. We firmly believe that, under their leadership and with the effective intervention of the concerned authorities, all necessary steps will be taken to ensure the safety and security of film industry personalities and to prevent the recurrence of such alarming incidents," the release stated.FWICE asks for security for Tiger Shroff and familyDemanding protection for the actor and his family, FWICE added, "We look forward to decisive action that will restore a sense of security and confidence among the members of the film fraternity. Furthermore, FWICE earnestly requests the police authorities to provide adequate security and protection to Tiger Shroff and his family, considering the seriousness of the incident and the concerns arising from such repeated acts of violence."The federation emphasised that actors, directors, producers and technicians must be able to carry out their professional responsibilities without fear or criminal intimidation."The film industry contributes significantly to the cultural identity, employment and economy of our country. Its members must be able to carry out their professional and personal activities without fear, threats or intimidation. Repeated incidents of this nature are creating unnecessary fear and insecurity among actors, directors, producers and other members of the film fraternity," the release said.FWICE asks for preventive security measures for film industryFWICE also urged the Maharashtra government and Mumbai Police to introduce preventive security measures for members of the film industry following the incident."FWICE stands firmly against all forms of violence and criminal intimidation. We urge the Government and law enforcement agencies to take immediate and stringent action to prevent the recurrence of such incidents and restore confidence among the members of the film industry. We strongly condemn this cowardly act and reiterate that the safety and security of every member of the film fraternity must be treated as a matter of utmost priority. FWICE remains hopeful that the Mumbai Police and the Government of Maharashtra will take all necessary measures to ensure that such incidents do not occur again," the release noted.Meanwhile, following the firing incident, Tiger Shroff's sister, Krishna Shroff, arrived at the actor's residence. Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde also visited the actor.Eyewitness narates shooting incidentAn eyewitness to the incident, Shalma Shaikh, said the firing took place shortly after 7 pm, following a football match at the ground. She recalled that the initial gunshots were mistaken by people present at the spot for festive celebrations. However, the situation escalated when the vehicle suddenly stopped.According to Shaikh, Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt by ducking inside the vehicle, while his personal driver sustained gunshot injuries. "My name is Shalma Shaikh, and I run a blog called 'Shalma Shaikh Blog.' For this, I travel all over Mumbai, capturing content. Sundays, however, follow a set routine: I film Amitabh, then Tiger, then Abhishek. Today, once the football match ended, everyone started filming. I called out to Tiger. He got into the car and drove off. As soon as he reached the main road, a boy started firing a gun. At first, everyone thought it was just Diwali firecrackers. Then the car stopped, and Tiger was on the floor. He didn't get a single scratch. However, his driver was struck; a bullet hit his elbow, and one passed right through his palm. They immediately rushed to the police station, and from there, they came to Nanavati Hospital. Everyone else from his family has since left, but the driver, the patient, is still inside. Their game usually ends at 7. By 7:05, they typically come out and head home," she said.The incident also triggered political reactions, with various members of the opposition questioning the alleged involvement of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.About the firing incident involving Tiger ShroffEarlier, Mumbai Police said that three to four rounds were fired at Tiger Shroff's vehicle as he was leaving a ground on Sunday. A large crowd had gathered to see the actor when several rounds were fired at his car from within the crowd.According to the police, Tiger Shroff was not hit by any bullet and did not sustain any gunshot injuries. The incident was reported under the jurisdiction of Juhu Police Station. The actor is safe, while his driver sustained injuries in the firing.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: James McAvoy says he ‘nearly died’ after his lungs collapsed following botched biopsy
articles.summary: James McAvoy revealed how a "botched" lung biopsy nearly killed him and led to weeks in the hospital before he underwent an intense physical transformation for his "Glass" role.
articles.body: James McAvoy opened up about a life-threatening health scare that left him hospitalized for several weeks after what he described as a botched medical procedure. During a recent appearance on Dax Shepard's "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 47-year-old actor recalled how he pushed his body to its limits for his transformation into the Beast in 2019's "Glass" after first recovering from a serious infection and collapsed lungs. "I'd actually been in hospital and I had a lung puncture because… they saw a shadow in my lung, so they wanted to biopsy it to see if it was cancer, which it wasn't, which was great," McAvoy said. "But that was botched, and I nearly died," he continued. "I was at home two days later and my lungs just collapsed in bed one night, and I was on my own as well, so it was crazy." SHARON STONE CLAIMS EX-HUSBAND SIGNED HER UP FOR BRAIN SURGERY WITHOUT HER CONSENT AFTER STROKE The "X-Men: First Class" star said he spent two or three weeks in the hospital while doctors worked unsuccessfully to clear his lungs. "They tried everything to clean out," McAvoy recalled. "Nothing was working. So, they were like, 'We're going to need to cut you open big-style. Go in with like soapy, like dish soap basically, and just like clean you out, scoop it all out.'" McAvoy recalled that after his medical ordeal, he underwent an intense process for the next four or five months as he bulked up to reprise his role in "Glass." In the M. Night Shyamalan-directed movie, the actor portrayed Kevin Wendell Crumb, who suffers from severe dissociative identity disorder (DID) with 24 distinct personalities. MATT DAMON REFUSES TO PUT BODY IN 'DANGEROUS' SITUATIONS FOR HOLLYWOOD ROLES AFTER TURNING 50 McAvoy first played Wendell in 2016's "Split," which was the sequel to 2000's "Unbreakable." In "Split," Wendell's 24th personality "The Beast," who possesses superhuman strength, speed, durability and pain suppression, became the central threat after emerging toward the end of the film. "Unlike ‘Split,’ I was the Beast, like most of the movie," McAvoy recalled. "So I was like, 'I'm really going to need to do the real thing. I'm going to need to go for it.'" 'THE ODYSSEY' STAR MATT DAMON REVEALS BRUTAL SIX-MONTH TRANSFORMATION BEHIND CHRISTOPHER NOLAN FILM "I remember saying to [Shyamalan] like, ‘You’re going to need to get me a trainer,'" he said. McAvoy explained that Shyamalan offered to hire a trainer from "the local gym," but he rejected that idea. 'SUITS' STAR RICK HOFFMAN REVEALS 'INTENSE' ROUTINE BEHIND DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION McAvoy said he had worked with trainers from local gyms before but needed someone who could transform his physique into that of a figure from Greek mythology. "The guy that worked with me was amazing," he added. "He didn't move in with me, but he was just with me a lot and kind of regulated what I ate and trained me just right." SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH STRUGGLE BEHIND HIS FAMOUSLY RIPPED PHYSIQUE "For the first four weeks, he rehabilitated me. I could walk, but I couldn’t run, couldn’t cycle, couldn’t jog," McAvoy recalled. "So he did a lot of rehabilitation and, sort of, functional movement, and then put the pounds on me really fast." McAvoy recently claimed that he was bullied on the set of the hit HBO miniseries "Band of Brothers." 'BLIND SIDE' STAR QUINTON AARON SAYS HE 'SAW JESUS' WHILE IN A COMA AFTER NEAR-FATAL STROKE While recently appearing on "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen," McAvoy was asked to rate his experience working on different projects, and when he was shown a picture of the show's cast, he recalled that one of his co-stars organized a group to mock him on set. And all these guys were in it for nine months, 10 months, and they get one line in one episode, and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines." articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes movie ‘You Can See Everything’ is a hit in theaters
articles.summary: While Paramount’s “Street Fighter” took the first-place spot at the box office, most of the attention — and cultural discourse — was on the Holmes documentary.
articles.body: North American movie theaters were flooded with new films this weekend, including a video game reboot, a big-budget survival thriller and a Jane Austen adaptation. While Paramount’s “Street Fighter” took the first-place spot, earning $31 million from 3,575 theaters according to studio estimates on Sunday, most of the attention and cultural discourse was elsewhere: on the nearly three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary, “You Can See Everything.” ‘You Can See Everything’ had thousands of sellouts Buzz and box office don’t always line up, but “You Can See Everything” made an extraordinary $15 million from only 855 screens, with over 2,000 sellout showings over the weekend, according to A24. It also had the biggest opening for a film playing on under 1,000 screens since “Borat” opened to $26.5 million in 2006, and the biggest nonmusic documentary opening in two decades, since “Fahrenheit 9/11” made nearly $24 million from 868 theaters. Those numbers do not account for inflation. Like other hits this year, like the Gen Z-driven “Backrooms” and “Obsession,” ticket sales for “You Can See Everything” were driven by a largely younger audience. Over 70% of the opening weekend crowd was under 35. The film, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, was made in secret over three years. Fielder spent over a month with the disgraced Theranos founder and her family, including two young children and partner Billy Evans, in her final days before reporting to federal prison. The reviews have been extremely positive, with 99% on Rotten Tomatoes and 99 on Metacritic. It also got an unprecedented 91% “definite recommend” from audiences, according to PostTrak exit polls. “You Can See Everything” reportedly cost under $7 million to make and less than $10 million to market. “Everybody underestimated the movie, because on paper this is like, wait, a three-hour documentary?” said Paul Dergarabedian, the head of marketplace trends for Rentrak. “But he (Fielder) is a huge draw, and he has a huge following on social media, and then Elizabeth Holmes is just a character that you couldn’t even make up. It’s stranger than fiction, and that’s really compelling.” ‘Street Fighter’ knocks out ‘Whalefall’ “Street Fighter” topped the charts as expected with a $51 million global opening, including $20 million from international showings. The movie starring Callina Liang, Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji cost a reported $82 million to make, not accounting for marketing and promotion. Audiences were 69% male. Both “Street Fighter” and “You Can See Everything” may have contributed to “Whalefall’s” relative failure this weekend. The $60 million survival thriller starring Austin Abrams and Josh Brolin made $8 million from 3,065 locations in the U.S. and Canada, despite being better reviewed than “Street Fighter.” With $9.5 million from international showings, the Disney release had a $17.5 million global launch. “Whalefall” opened in fourth place, behind the Jessica Chastain horror “Other Mommy.” The Universal Pictures release added $8.4 million in its second weekend, bringing its domestic total to $44.9 million. Fifth place went to “Sense and Sensibility,” which earned an estimated $7.3 million from 2,545 theaters. The well-reviewed Austen adaptation starring Daisy Edgar-Jones drew a predominantly younger (58% between the ages of 14 and 18) and female crowd (84%). It also got the strongest CinemaScore of the week (A-). Warner Bros. Clockwork also released a restored presentation of Ken Russell’s 1971 film “The Devils” in 350 locations, where it made $1.6 million. It’s the first release from the studio’s specialty label. ‘Musk’ documentary facing advertising blocks and Netflix shares box office for ‘La Bola Negra’ Alex Gibney's Elon Musk documentary “Musk” also expanded to 472 screens in the U.S. and Canada, where it made $306,702. The film, which runs nearly four hours, has faced issues advertising on major social media platforms including X, which Musk owns, and TikTok, according to distributor Bleecker Street, which said TikTok this weekend permanently suspended the film’s ad account. Netflix also shared ticket sales for the first time for the queer Spanish epic “La Bola Negra,” which made $277,500 from four locations this weekend. The streamer has not historically reported box office for its theatrical releases, but this film is breaking new ground as it's being positioned as a possible best picture contender. It will be in theaters for 47 days before it will be available to watch on Netflix. According to Rentrak, the weekend overall generated about $101.6 million in ticket sales, up 45% from the same weekend last year. The year to date stands at $8.2 billion, which is up almost 20% from 2025. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Street Fighter,” $31 million. 2. “You Can See Everything,” $15 million. 3. “Other Mommy,” $8.4 million. 4. “Whalefall,” $8 million. 5. “Sense and Sensibility,” $7.3 million. 6. “Verity,” $6.2 million. 7. “Resident Evil,” $5.5 million. 8. “Heart of the Beast,” $4.8 million. 9. “Jailer 2,” $3.2 million. 10. “Forgotten Island,” $2.3 million.
