articles.title: Kristin Cavallari says she learned a painful $250K lesson involving her father at 22
articles.summary: Kristin Cavallari revealed on her podcast how two six-figure loans to her father Dennis Cavallari were never repaid, leaving her $250,000 in the hole.
articles.body: Kristin Cavallari is reflecting on a painful lesson after lending her father a quarter of a million dollars. During a recent episode of her podcast "Let's Be Honest with Kristin Cavallari," in which the 39-year-old reality star shared her opinions on women and finances, Cavallari recalled how she ended up $250,000 "in the hole" following two loans to her father Dennis Cavallari that were never repaid. "My dad came to me — I was filming ‘The Hills,’ so I must have been 22 — and asked for a large sum of money to borrow. Six figures," she said. KRISTIN CAVALLARI ADMITS HER KIDS FLY COACH WHILE SHE SITS IN FIRST CLASS "And I was making great money at the time, but it’s still — I’m 22," Cavallari continued. "Six figures is a big deal for me." "But I lent it to him, and he promised me he would pay me back," the Uncommon James founder remembered. "He probably said six months, and he was going to give me interest on top of it. And, you know, well, I didn’t get paid back. And instead, he asked to borrow more money, another six-figure number." JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER CLAIMS HER EX-HUSBAND SECRETLY STOLE HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS FROM HER 'SOPRANOS' EARNINGS Cavallari said that she confronted Dennis about not repaying the first loan but ultimately relented. "I said to him, ‘You haven’t even acknowledged the first payment, and now you want more money?’" she recalled. "But because I’m such a f-----g sucker — or I was at the time — I lent him more money." WYNONNA JUDD ADMITS HELPING DAUGHTER DURING METH BATTLE ‘BIT ME IN THE BUTT' The "Laguna Beach" alum admitted she has no expectation of ever getting the money back. "I will never see that money," she said. "So, when I tell you, I’m in the hole with my own dad, a quarter of a million dollars." THE RICH HAVE ONE FINANCIAL HABIT MOST AMERICANS IGNORE AT THEIR PERIL "Talk about a bad business decision," Cavallari added. However, the TV personality acknowledged that the experience taught her the importance of setting boundaries with family and friends when it comes to money. JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME "I didn’t know how to set boundaries in my early 20s," she admitted. "I’ve learned that. You know, it would be a very different conversation probably today, but it’s the lending-money-to-people thing." "When you have money, it’s almost like people expect it," Cavallari continued. "And you are in no way, shape or form required or obligated to lend anybody money, especially if you’ve worked your f---king tail off for that money." JENNIFER GARNER SAYS SHE 'PANICKED' ABOUT FINANCIAL STABILITY AFTER DIVORCE FROM BEN AFFLECK "Like I have worked my ass off for all of my money," she added. "And so I think that’s why probably that stings the most." "It just was like sort of taking advantage of me at such a young age." CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT Now a mother herself, Cavallari said she struggles to understand her father's decision to turn to her for such a large sum of money when she was so young. Cavallari shares sons Camden, 14, and Jaxon, 12, and daughter Saylor, 10, with her ex-husband, former NFL quarterback Jay Cutler. JENNIFER GARNER SAYS DIVORCE FROM BEN AFFLECK CAUSED 'UPHEAVAL' THAT KEPT HER FROM WORKING FOR YEARS "I can’t imagine going to my kids when they’re 22 and asking for that kind of money," she said. "I guess I understand that he didn’t have a lot of options. But I don't know." "And also my relationship with my dad is very complicated," Cavallari continued. "So there are other layers to it. But for the purpose of this conversation, I just think you’re allowed to do what you want to do with your money." Cavallari shared a clip from the episode on Instagram, emphasizing the importance of financial literacy for women. "We’re talking all things MONEY this week!!" she wrote. "I’m over money being a taboo topic for women. We’re talking financial independence, the mistakes I’ve made, and everything I’ve learned along the way. If you wanna chase the bag, this one’s for you." Cavallari previously discussed her difficult relationship with Dennis and the unpaid loans during a July appearance on the "Aspire with Emma Grede" podcast. The "Balancing in Heels" author shared that she eventually came to terms with the financial loss. "I've had to grapple with it, you know, and I've ultimately put it to bed and made peace with it," she said. "I think at the time, I didn't know how to say no to my dad. That's also been sort of like a big life lesson for me. I mean, I've ultimately cut my dad out of my life." And so, that's probably like the biggest thing that stands out in my mind in terms of how you think about teaching your kids about money." articles.title: 7 held for Kolkata stampede; ‘pandal collapse warning’ triggered run?
articles.summary: KOLKATA: A suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder was filed and seven people, two of them office-bearers of Chorbagan Durga Puja
articles.body: KOLKATA: A suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder was filed and seven people, two of them office-bearers of Chorbagan Durga Puja committee, were arrested for Saturday night’s stampede amid heavy rain at the north Kolkata pandal that led to 19 deaths and injuries to 24.CM Suvendu Adhikari promised a judicial probe headed by a sitting judge, subject to the chief justice’s approval, or a retired judge, and pledged to make its findings public. He announced Rs 5 lakh for each injured person and said a magistrate-rank officer and a DSP-rank officer would accompany each victim’s body home.The crush occurred around 7.30pm on Saptami, after an announcement allegedly warning that the pandal’s structure might collapse sent visitors rushing for the exits. Several people fell down stairs near the exit and were trampled. One of the 24 injured remains critical.Police arrested puja committee secretary Rajkumar Seoda, vice-president Shantanu Dubey, Biplab Mukhopadhyay, responsible for installing the bamboo structure, crowd managers Kaushik Saha and Pintu De, and private security agency employees Suman Chakraborty and Rajesh Pal.A special investigation team is examining CCTV footage and eyewitness accounts to establish who made the announcement and why.“We have gathered sufficient evidence pointing to gross mismanagement by the puja organisers. There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors, and everything was handled verbally,” a senior Kolkata police officer said.Residents described panic and inadequate crowd control. "People panicked when organisers started announcing that the pandal might cave in. That caused the stampede," said Ramji Sau, a resident. Beauty Naskar alleged there was hardly any police or volunteers controlling the crowd, with some young volunteers busy on their phones.Adhikari said temporary home guards managing ropes separating entry and exit routes abandoned their posts when rain began. He directed police across Bengal to inspect major pandals, restrict entry where necessary and enforce safety measures.A total of nine IPS officers with previous Kolkata police experience have been assigned puja duty in the city. Police have been instructed to keep exits clear, improve lighting, maintain crowd movement and carry ropes, guardrails and loudspeakers.The tragedy brought Trinamool, CPM and Congress together at Girish Park police station, where they demanded accountability and questioned why senior organisers and officials responsible for lapses had not been arrested. The opposition threatened larger protests after the festival.West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar and Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh called the arrests an "eyewash", while CPM demanded that those who had prioritised control of the puja committee over visitor safety be brought to justice.BJP Bengal president Samik Bhattacharya appealed against political recriminations, saying the priority should be supporting bereaved families and bringing those responsible to justice. The Ritabrata Banerjee faction of Trinamool echoed the appeal, saying: "Puja isn't the time for politics."Adhikari defended his govt's response and accused previous administrations of withholding inquiry commission reports. Referring to past disasters, he asked: "Have you ever seen a chief minister spending the entire night at a hospital?" he added.Across Kolkata, puja committees scrambled to improve safety, increase lighting, deploy volunteers and fire tenders, clear exits and limit number of visitors inside pandals. Santosh Mitra Square adopted staggered entry and increased volunteers. Thakurpukur SB Park cut its permitted crowd from 200-250 to about 100 at a time.On Sunday, queues continued at popular pandals, including Md Ali Park and College Square. articles.title: Kevin Bacon pleads for help recovering missing FedEx package rerouted multiple times around the globe
articles.summary: Kevin Bacon's FedEx package of sentimental '90s clothes was shipped to Israel instead of Ireland and bounced through multiple countries since.
articles.body: Kevin Bacon was yearning and burning for somebody to tell him where his lost clothes were hiding. Bacon, 68, pleaded with his followers to help him figure out where FedEx sent a package of clothing he sent last month to a location across the pond. "Hey everybody, it's me. I'm over here, I'm working in Ireland," Bacon told his followers. "I wanted to pack light, so I decided to ship some old clothes over here to Ireland. I don't buy a lot of clothes. I've had these clothes probably since the '90s. 'FOOTLOOSE' STAR KEVIN BACON SHARES HOW THE MOVIE STILL HAUNTS HIM "So I used a shipping service that I don't want to say the name but it rhymes with BreadX," he said before explaining that he shipped a box of clothing on Sept. 26 from upstate New York to his filming location. "It went straight to Memphis, and then from Memphis it to France and by Sept. 28 it arrived in Germany, and by Sept. 29, they shipped it straight to Israel, not Ireland – Israel." The "Footloose" actor went on to explain that the package traveled from Israel back to France on Oct. 3, only to be sent back to Israel the following day. It traveled to Germany on Oct. 5 before being routed back to Israel on Oct. 6. KEVIN BACON'S DREAM OF BEING A FARMER LED TO 'BIGGEST FIGHT' WITH WIFE KYRA SEDGWICK "On Oct. 10, that box of old clothes made its way all the way to France, and on Oct. 11 it arrived in the UK, in England," he said. "Pretty close. Guess what? On Oct. 11, it left the UK and came straight to Ireland, where it has been sitting for five days, and they say they're unable to deliver it." articles.title: Colours Of Navaratri - Day 9: When blue meets green, and art finds its hue
articles.summary: Art, much like the peacock blue-green she wears, refuses to be defined by a single shade.
articles.body: Art, much like the peacock blue-green she wears, refuses to be defined by a single shade. For violinist Shreya Devnath, it is about perception, evolution and staying true to oneself. As the final day of Navaratri draws to a close, she reflects on how art can evolve with time without ever losing its soul.Navaratri is a season of music, devotion and celebration. Beyond concerts and performances, what does the festival mean to you personally?Navaratri is a very joyous time for me. Growing up, my grandmother would create an entire village of Gokulam at home, sometimes with elaborate, room-by-room storytelling. Even before concerts, my earliest association with Navaratri was the joy of imagining something and bringing it to life. It was practically Disneyland!There's such a strong visual identity to a Navratri concert. From the saris and jewellery to flowers and the overall atmosphere, what part of that visual tradition do you connect with the most?Onstage, definitely the saris. Having a colour for each day brings people together, and anything that brings people together is a form of love. Offstage, it is the kolu displays. Every home reflects its owner’s imagination and childhood; you see someone’s kolu and immediately feel you know them a little better.Can what a musician wears influence how they feel or perform onstage?Absolutely. Everything about you finds expression in your music — your state of mind, what you wear, how you feel in it, even what you see on the way to a concert. Everything tangible and intangible finds its way into the music, if you allow it to flow. Fashion is no exception to that.Your peacock blue-green sarishifts shades with the light. Does this duality resonate with you as an artist?I think that is the essence of art. Two people can listen to the same piece of music and interpret it differently. Even the same person might experience it differently ten years later. It is all about perception. Today, this colour is green; tomorrow, it is blue. That, to me, defines art itself.If your musical personality were a wardrobe, what would it look like?Nature-themed, definitely. I feel deeply connected to nature — standing under a tree, talking to the moon or being by the ocean. I loved that this sari had a peacock on it, so I picked it straight away.Finally, whose personal style in the Carnatic music world do you admire, and what makes it work?MS amma. Her style reflected what was inside her; it wasn’t simply about what was in vogue. It reflected who she was and what her music stood for. When we are entirely swayed by external trends and try too hard to fit in, the irony is that we end up belonging nowhere. Fashion works when what you show on the outside is what you truly are on the inside.STYLE FILELet peacock green take centre stage with jewel-toned pairings and heritage details.Play with contrast: Pair peacock green with royal blue, deep purple or antique gold.Make it a drape: Let a rich silk saree with a traditional border do the talking.Bring on the gold: Temple jewellery, antique jhumkas and gold bangles add timeless grandeur.Finish with flowers: A string of mallipoo lends a fresh, traditional touch.Peacock green is rich enough to command attention; let the jewellery complement, not competeBEAUTY FILEJewel-toned elegance meets luminous skin and eyes that captivate.Define the eyes: Try emerald liner or smoky eyes with bronze and gold shimmer.Glow strategically: Warm gold highlighter on the cheekbones complements the richness of the colour.Find your lip shade: Pair the look with berry, brick-red or a muted rose lip.Seal it with a bindi: A small maroon or deep green bindi adds a classic finishing touchLet the eyes carry the drama with bronze and gold; keep the skin fresh and luminousWritten By: Aashna ReddyGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Cynthia Erivo helps fund the next generation of performers with a USC drama scholarship and a companion film bursary at Oxford
articles.summary: Success on stage and screen often depends on the people who open doors at the right moment.
articles.body: Success on stage and screen often depends on the people who open doors at the right moment. Cynthia Erivo knows that well, and now she is opening them for others. The Tony Award winner and Academy Award nominee has lent her name and her voice to a new scholarship for a drama student at the University of Southern California School of Dramatic Arts, unveiled at an event in Oxford. A companion film award was announced for students at the University of Oxford. Here’s who funded the scholarship, who received it, and what Erivo told the next generation.Cynthia Erivo Scholarship, what the University of Southern California School of Dramatic Arts unveiledThe University of Southern California School of Dramatic Arts announced the Cynthia Erivo Scholarship in May 2026, describing it as an award established to support a student at the school, which has prepared generations of theatre artists in one of the world's major entertainment hubs. According to the school's announcement, the scholarship honours one of the most celebrated performers of her generation, a Tony Award winner and Academy Award nominee known for transformative roles and increasingly for advocating equity and opportunity in Hollywood. The school says that mix of artistry and advocacy is what the award aims to celebrate and inspire. Dean Emily Roxworthy told the school's community in the announcement that Erivo represents the craft, fearless storytelling, and sense of responsibility the school hopes to cultivate, adding that opportunity is a starting point rather than a finish line.Cynthia Erivo, Doctor Stacy L. Smith, and the inaugural Icon Award 2026The scholarship was unveiled on May 5, 2026, at an event at the University of Oxford, in the Sohmen Concert Hall of the Stephen A. Schwarzman Centre for the Humanities. The school's announcement says Erivo joined Dr Stacy L. Smith of the University of Southern California Annenberg Inclusion Initiative for a wide-ranging conversation about storytelling, creativity, and the future of entertainment. At the same event, Erivo received the inaugural Icon Award from the Annenberg Inclusion Initiative, and Dean Roxworthy travelled to Oxford to mark the occasion. Smith, who has spent decades documenting barriers facing underrepresented voices in the industry, told the audience that Erivo's work, advocacy, and ethos are resonant and necessary today, and called her commitment to supporting the next generation of filmmakers extraordinary. For attendees, the evening linked an acclaimed career with a practical gesture of support.The Adobe Foundation, Jason and Yvonne Huff Lee, and a companion Film Bursary at OxfordAccording to the announcement, the scholarship is designed to support multihyphenate students pursuing careers across film, theatre, and the creative industries, meaning students who work in several roles at once. It is funded by the Adobe Foundation, Jason and Yvonne Huff Lee, the University of Southern California School of Dramatic Arts, and the University of Southern California Annenberg Inclusion Initiative. Such a mix of corporate, individual, and institutional backing shows how scholarships of this kind often depend on several partners working together. The school also announced a companion award, the Cynthia Erivo Film Bursary, for students at the University of Oxford, created in partnership with the Schwarzman Centre. A bursary is a financial award that supports a student's studies, so the two honours together extend Erivo's name and support across both sides of the Atlantic, from California to Oxford.Meet Brooklyn Norrington, the Master of Fine Arts in Acting student who received the 2026 scholarshipThe scholarship's recipient is Brooklyn Norrington, a rising third-year Master of Fine Arts in Acting student at the University of Southern California School of Dramatic Arts, according to the announcement. This season, Norrington has appeared in two campus productions: the new play Don't Feed the Pigeons, directed by David Warshofsky at the Dick Wolf Drama Centre's Sanctuary Theatre, and Twelfth Night, directed by Kate Burton and Paul Urcioli at the Bing Theatre. Norrington travelled to Oxford for the announcement, accompanied by her parents, and received the 2026 Cynthia Erivo Scholarship Award from Erivo and Dean Roxworthy at the event. For aspiring actors reading this story, the profile is a useful reminder that scholarship recipients are working performers already building credits, and that financial support can help them keep training while they do so.Cynthia Erivo's message to students, be purposeful, be ready for the yeses, and never copy someone elseErivo's own path shaped her commitment. According to the school's announcement, she told the audience at the Schwarzman Centre that her training at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art was not without difficulties, and that those experiences became the foundation for serving that school as an alumna. She said she wanted to ensure no one else had that experience, and that she did not want her involvement to be nominal, "I wanted to be purposeful." She also said she wants those who come after her to be supported as they should be. Her advice for students was practical, be ready for the yeses, because the noes are easy while the yeses demand readiness. She closed with a reminder to students that each of them is made singularly and should not try to become someone else.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
